Lying still in an enclosed space at around 20°C, a person still loses about 1.8 L of water a day through breath and skin (scaled by body weight); heavy work, shouting and coughing in the dust all cost more. Losing water equal to more than 6% of body weight starts to do damage; more than 15% is fatal. Under the rubble, thirst kills first, not hunger.
strings.一块松动的砖头掉下来，砸在 {actor} 的胳膊上。: A loose brick drops and lands on {actor}’s arm.
strings.一小包一小包的药和绷带顺着缝塞了进来。: Small packets of pills and bandages came down through the gap.
strings.一把拽住蛇皮袋，把大家喊醒: Grab the sack and wake everyone
strings.一条黄毛的中华田园犬，三十来斤重。五年前老刘在大厦地下车库里捡到它，从此它天天跟: A yellow Chinese village dog, about 15 kg. Dustin found him in the tower’s underground garage five years ago; since then he has followed him on his rounds every day, and property management never managed to chase him off. He was with Dustin on the stairs to the third floor when the quake hit; a shard of glass opened his left front paw, and he has been lying beside Dustin ever since.
strings.一栋 12 层的写字楼整体坍塌。会议室里一块斜塌下来的楼板搭在会议桌和铁皮文件柜: A 12-story office building has collapsed completely. In the conference room, a slab has come down at an angle across the conference table and a steel filing cabinet, propping open a triangular gap about four metres long and less than 1.2 metres high at its tallest.
strings.一次 6 级上下的强余震！整片废墟都在往下坐，三角区里的人被颠得撞在一起，头顶传: A strong aftershock, around magnitude 6! The whole ruin settles downward, the people in the triangle are thrown into each other, and overhead comes the twang of rebar snapping.
strings.一次给足半升多；之后各安天命: More than half a litre in one go; after that, each to their fate
strings.一点电都不浪费，但干活摸黑，也收不到任何消息: Not a drop of power wasted — but the work is done in the dark, and no message can get through
strings.一直跟他说话，别让他睡过去: Keep talking to him, don’t let him sleep
strings.一股带着雨腥味的凉风从洞口灌了进来。大家轮流趴在洞口，对着那丝天光敲、喊。: A cold draught with the smell of rain pours in through the gap. They take turns lying at the opening, knocking and shouting at that thread of daylight.
strings.一视同仁，谁也不能多拿: The same for everyone; no one gets more
strings.一起大喊，让狗叫起来: Shout together, get the dog barking
strings.一部手机一直亮着，被放在离裂缝最近的地方。所有人时不时就看它一眼。: One phone stays lit, set down closest to the crack. Everyone glances at it, over and over.
strings.七六年我在底下埋了三天，那年才九岁。你们比我那会儿强多了。: In ’76 I was under a building for three days. I was nine. You’re doing better than I was.
strings.三楼东侧的会议室没有被完全压扁：一块斜塌下来的楼板搭在会议桌和铁皮文件柜上，撑出: The conference room on the east side of the third floor was not crushed flat. A slab came down at an angle across the conference table and a steel filing cabinet, propping open a triangular gap about four metres long and less than 1.2 metres high at its tallest. Six people are trapped inside: the owner, the accountant and the intern of Hongyuan, a delivery rider who had come with afternoon tea, a rival who had come to “talk partnership”, and Dustin, the building’s security guard — along with Buddy, the yellow mutt that follows him on his rounds. Dustin’s shins are pinned fast under a slab. Buddy lies beside him, whimpering, again and again.
strings.三角区的一角整个塌了下来，{actor} 正好缩在那一边。: One corner of the triangle collapses entirely, and {actor} was curled up on that side.
strings.三角区里安静了很久。然后有人把自己的外套盖在了 {actor} 身上。: The triangle goes quiet for a long moment. Then someone lays their jacket over {actor}.
strings.三角区里已经很久没有人说话了。会议桌底下还压着那天开会用的会议纪要。有人摸黑撕下: Nobody in the triangle has spoken for a long time. Under the conference table, the meeting notes from that day are still there. Someone tears a sheet off in the dark and says, quietly, “Let’s each write a few lines… for the people at home. In case…” Nobody finishes that sentence.
strings.三角区里的空气一下子绷紧了。: The air in the triangle goes taut at once.
strings.上一次余震晃起来的时候，周敏的第一反应不是护住头，而是死死抱住她那个黑色公文包。: The last time an aftershock hit, Michelle Zhou’s first move was not to cover her head but to clamp both arms around the black briefcase. {actor} saw it.
strings.上面夹缝里的声音一次比一次小。朵朵说她好渴，好怕，吴老师的手越来越凉，她想下来。: The voice from the gap overhead gets smaller each time. Daisy says she is so thirsty, and so scared, and Teacher Wu’s hand is getting colder and colder, and she wants to come down.
strings.上面所有的机器突然都停了，连人声都没有了。过了一会儿，扩音器里一个沙哑的声音：“: Every machine above suddenly stops, and even the voices stop. After a moment a hoarse voice comes over the megaphone: “Silence for listening! Is anyone down there? Knock three times if you can hear me!”
strings.上面的夹缝里传来朵朵的一声尖叫，接着是压抑的哭声。: From the gap above comes a single scream from Daisy, and then muffled crying.
strings.下雨时，雨水会顺着楼板的裂缝一滴滴渗下来。撑开倒置的雨伞、摆好杯子和文件盒去接（: When it rains, water drips down through the cracks in the slab. Open the umbrella upside down, set out cups and document boxes to catch it (there is only room for two people under the leak). Someone has to stay at the leak, and their clothes will be soaked through; water that has filtered through rubble is not clean either.
strings.不会说话。呜咽、低吼，偶尔冲着外面叫两声。: He doesn’t speak. Whimpers, growls low, and sometimes barks twice at the outside.
strings.不写：写了就是认命: Don’t write: writing it means giving up
strings.不动楼板；她一个人在上面会越来越怕: The slab stays untouched; she will only get more frightened, alone
strings.不喝，再忍忍: Don’t drink. Hold out a little longer.
strings.不想给大家添麻烦: You don’t want to be a burden
strings.不撬，等救援队来输了液再说: Don’t pry; wait for the rescue team and an IV
strings.不添麻烦；可水还是那么一口，活还是要干: No trouble for anyone; but the water is still one mouthful, and the work still needs doing
strings.不用再等了，可楼梯间随时可能二次坍塌；爬不动的人和被压着的老刘只能留下: No more waiting — but the stairwell could come down again at any moment; those who can’t crawl, and Dustin, pinned, have to stay
strings.不用吊，下面就不会大塌；可通道要多挖好几个钟头，电锤震得楼板一直在抖，他得一直守: No lift, no big collapse; but the tunnel takes hours longer, the hammer shakes the slab without stopping, and he has to stay down here the whole time
strings.不给别人添麻烦: Don’t be a burden to anyone
strings.不能拖累大家，咬着牙接着干: Do not be a burden. Grit your teeth and keep working
strings.不能搬，等救援队来输了液再说: Don’t move him; wait for the rescue team and an IV
strings.不费什么，但也只能知道她还活着: Costs almost nothing — but all it tells you is that she is still alive
strings.不费水，只能听天由命: Costs no water — and there is nothing to do but wait and hope
strings.不输了，两袋盐水大家分着喝: No IV — split both bags of saline and drink it
strings.东墙终于被掏穿了。墙后的消防楼梯间塌了一半，钢筋像乱麻一样支棱着。可顺着歪斜的楼: The east wall is finally broken through. Behind it the fire stairwell has half collapsed, rebar sticking out like tangled hemp. But looking up the crooked stairs there is a thread of grey daylight, and voices from outside, faint but there.
strings.东头那一截楼板整个坐了下来。西头的人缩成一团，听着东边的动静。: The whole east end of the slab comes down. Huddled in the west, they listen to the sounds from the east.
strings.东西在自己手里才踏实: It is only real when it is in your own hands
strings.两个人的秘密一起揭开: Two people’s secrets come apart together
strings.两支强光手电被塞了进来。三角区第一次被照得这么亮——每个人都被彼此的样子吓了一跳: Two powerful flashlights were passed down. For the first time the triangle is lit up — and everyone is startled by how the others look.
strings.两条小腿都没保住。装上假肢以后，老刘回了达州乡下，在镇口开了个小卖部。有人问起他: Neither shin could be saved. Once he had his prosthetics, Dustin went back to the Dazhou countryside and opened a little shop at the mouth of the town. When people ask about his legs he says, “Buried under Jinhua Tower. Held the ceiling up for the people inside for a few days.” Then he laughs before anyone else can.
strings.两条皮带一左一右勒进了老刘的大腿。他咬着一团布，一声没吭。: Two belts were cinched tight around Dustin’s thighs, one on each side. He bit down on a rag and made no sound at all.
strings.两瓶喝了一半的矿泉水，一个保温杯里的凉茶。: Two half-drunk bottles of mineral water and a thermos of herbal tea.
strings.举着手机找信号: Hold a phone up for a signal
strings.九楼那家公司开追悼会那天，门口的签到台上多了一部屏幕裂了的手机，装在塑料袋里，袋: On the day the ninth-floor company held its memorial service, a phone with a cracked screen appeared on the signing-in table at the door, in a plastic bag with a name written on it in marker pen. Nobody saw who left it.
strings.也许是本能，可这会让头顶更不稳: Instinct, maybe — but it will make the ceiling less stable
strings.事故调查报告把责任归给了房东和监理。何志强在电视上感谢救援队，说“是大家互相扶持: The accident report laid the blame on the landlord and the site supervisor. On television Steven Ho thanked the rescue teams and said, “We lived because we held each other up.” That night he got drunk and sat alone in his living room, reaching up to touch the ceiling, over and over.
strings.事故调查组找他做了三次笔录。他手绘的那张受力分析图，和“原图纸只有十层”的证词，: The investigation interviewed him three times. His hand-drawn load diagram, and his testimony that the original drawings show ten floors, became key evidence in the report. Huacheng took the south-city project. He resigned, and went to work as an ordinary engineer at a structural inspection firm.
strings.五月中旬，一个闷热的下午。两点四十一分，地面先是猛地往上一顶，接着左右狂甩。城南: Mid-May, a sultry afternoon. At 2:41 the ground gave a violent heave upward, then whipped from side to side. On the south side of the city, the twelve-story Jinhua Tower seemed to lose its spine and sank down, each floor folding onto the one below.
strings.五月的气温昼 24°C、夜 13°C，挤在一起不会冻死。但雨水从裂缝渗进来、衣服: May temperatures run 24°C by day and 13°C at night; huddled together, no one will freeze. But once rain seeps through the cracks and clothes are soaked, the nights bring shivering and burn a lot of extra calories. Rainwater that has filtered through the rubble is drinkable but not clean; drinking urine eases thirst for a while, at the cost of nausea and extra strain on the kidneys.
strings.人声最容易被确认，但喊完嗓子冒烟（每人多耗约 0.25 升水）: A human voice is the easiest thing to confirm, but shouting leaves throats raw (about 0.25 L of water each)
strings.什么也不改变；它还要喝大家的水: Nothing changes; and he drinks the water too
strings.什么也不用做；秦朗会记住谁没听他的: Nothing to do; Leonard Qin will remember who did not listen
strings.什么也不说，把脸埋进膝盖里: Say nothing, and bury your face in your knees
strings.什么也不说，自己尽量躺着别动: Say nothing, and lie as still as you can
strings.什么也不说，跟着他一起钻出去: Say nothing, and crawl out with him
strings.从东墙的裂口往消防楼梯间掏一条能爬过去的洞。楼梯间是混凝土核心筒，可能通向外面—: Cut a crawlable hole from the crack in the east wall through to the fire stairwell. The stairwell is the concrete core; it may lead outside — but every brick you take out makes the ceiling shift, and the dust gets worse.
strings.从东墙的裂口往消防楼梯间掏一条能爬过去的洞。楼梯间是混凝土核心筒，可能通向外面。: Dig a crawl-hole from the crack in the east wall through to the fire stairwell. The stairwell is a concrete core and may lead outside.
strings.从今天起给她多分一份水，什么活也不让她干: From today she gets an extra share of water and does no work at all
strings.从管道井里爬出去的人，在救护车上一遍一遍地对每一个穿制服的人说：“锦华大厦，三楼: The ones who crawled out through the pipe shaft told every uniformed person they saw, over and over, from the ambulance: “Jinhua Tower, east side of the third floor, there are still people.” The rescue teams dug at that ruin day after day. By the time the tunnel was through, nothing answered from the triangle. Alive: {survivors}. Left below: {dead}. Years later they still can’t ride in lifts, or go into any narrow place.
strings.从那以后，墙两边轮流说话：说孩子、说老家、说出去以后最想吃的那碗面。: From then on the two sides of the wall talk in turns: about their children, their home towns, the bowl of noodles they want most when they get out.
strings.他从管道井进来，就能从管道井出去；可一个趁乱翻东西的人，会去找警察扎堆的救援队吗: He came in through the pipe shaft, so he can go out the same way; but would a man rifling through the wreckage walk into a rescue camp full of police?
strings.他从管道井里钻出来的时候，膝盖和手肘全磨烂了。他没上救护车，一直蹲在车库口，给每: By the time he dragged himself out of the pipe shaft his knees and elbows were scraped raw. He refused the ambulance and crouched at the garage mouth, showing every rescue worker who went in the way to the east side of the third floor. Later the delivery platform gave him a “Best Rider” award. He didn’t keep a cent of it; he sent the whole sum to Dustin’s family in Dazhou.
strings.他们可能根本不会靠近: They may never come close at all.
strings.他们最清楚怎么接人: They know best how to bring people out
strings.他会记恨你: He will hold it against you
strings.他口袋里那张会议纪要上只写了两行字。第一行是给老婆的：“存折密码是儿子的生日。”: The meeting notes in his pocket held only two lines. The first was for his wife: “The passbook code is our son’s birthday.” The second had been crossed out and rewritten, rewritten and crossed out, until only three words were left: “I’m sorry.” No one knows who he meant them for.
strings.他多喝 0.4 升，你多一个靠山；被人看见就完了: He drinks 0.4 L more, you gain a patron; and if anyone sees, it’s over
strings.他拿走的也许只是几部手机；也许不只: What he takes may be only a few phones; or it may not
strings.他现在需要的不是问题: Questions are not what he needs now
strings.他的名字后来出现在两份文件上：一份是遇难者名单，一份是事故调查报告。那张签着他名: His name ended up in two documents: the list of the dead, and the accident investigation report. The acceptance certificate with his signature on it was locked away in a filing cabinet as evidence. The staff at Hongyuan pooled money for his funeral. Not many came.
strings.他袋子里有水、吃的、充电宝；他手里也有撬棍: There is water, food and a power bank in his sack; and he has a crowbar in his hand
strings.他说了算以后，每一处支撑都会有人盯着；何志强不会咽下这口气: With him in charge, every prop will be watched; Steven Ho will not swallow it
strings.他说只有瘦小的人挤得过去；爬出去的人能把救援队直接带过来，也可能卡死在半路: He says only a small, thin person can squeeze through; whoever goes can bring the rescuers straight here — or jam halfway and die
strings.他那份水会省下来给别人: His share of the water goes to someone else
strings.他那张会议纪要的一面画着一张受力分析图，标着三角区里哪根桌腿吃力最大；另一面只有: On one side of his meeting notes he had drawn a load diagram, marking which table leg in the triangle was taking the most weight; on the other side, a single line: “The original drawings show ten floors. Check.” That sheet of paper was later passed to his old sergeant from the army.
strings.他那张纸是写给女儿的，满纸错别字：“幺儿，爸爸答应你的视频，欠到起。生日蛋糕叫妈: His note was to his daughter, misspelled all the way through: “Little one, Papa owes you that video call. Tell Mama to buy the big birthday cake.” The station manager had the note laminated and hung it on the wall of the delivery station.
strings.会议室柜子里的办公室急救箱：纱布、绷带、碘伏、几片止痛药。: The office first-aid kit from the conference-room cabinet: gauze, bandages, iodine, a few painkillers.
strings.伤得最重的人先出去: The most badly injured go first
strings.何志强抢先开了口：“他是来抢项目的，什么话都编得出来！”三角区里吵成了一团，最后: Steven Ho gets in first: "He's here to steal a contract, he'll say anything!" The triangle erupts into shouting, and in the end nobody convinces anybody.
strings.何志强摸黑凑到领头人 {actor} 耳边，声音压得很低：“多分我一口水。出去以: Steven Ho gropes through the dark to the leader, {actor}, and keeps his voice very low: “Give me one extra mouthful of water. When we’re out, name your price, name whatever position you want. Steven Ho’s word is good.”
strings.何志强沉默了很久，开口的时候，声音哑得不像他自己的。: Steven Ho is silent for a long time. When he speaks, his voice is hoarse, not like his own.
strings.何志强的事会被揭开: What Steven Ho did will come out
strings.何志强说得很快，像是早就准备好了这句话。秦朗冷笑了一声，没再说话。: Steven Ho says it fast, as if the line had been ready a long time. Leonard Qin gives a cold laugh and says nothing more.
strings.余震一阵接一阵。外面的人知道锦华大厦塌了，可他们不知道，废墟下面还有人活着。: The aftershocks keep coming. The people outside know Jinhua Tower has fallen. They don’t know that anyone is still alive beneath it.
strings.余震中被楼板压住腿的人被压的小时数。: How many hours the person whose leg was pinned by a slab during an aftershock has been trapped.
strings.余震中，头顶的楼板猛地往下一沉，碎块和灰土劈头盖脸地砸了下来。: Mid-aftershock, the slab overhead drops with a jolt and debris and dust come down on everyone.
strings.余震把水桶晃倒了！桶身被一截钢筋戳出一个小口子，水正一股一股地往外冒。: The aftershock knocked the water jug over! A length of rebar has punched a small hole in the drum, and water is spurting out in pulses.
strings.余震按大森公式随时间衰减：每 8 小时发生一次有感强余震的概率 ≈ 10 ÷（震: Aftershocks die away over time according to Omori’s law: the chance of a strong, felt aftershock in any 8-hour stretch is ≈ 10 ÷ (hours since the quake + 14) — about 70% the first night, falling to just over 10% by the third day. Roughly a quarter of them are jolts of around magnitude 6 that can injure people, or even pin someone’s legs under a slab. Aftershocks lower the triangle’s integrity (its structural stability) and throw up dust; the lower the integrity, the likelier a collapse is to hurt someone. Digging and prying loosen the structure too. Dogs sense an earthquake’s primary wave (the P-wave) better than people do: while Buddy is with you, his few seconds of warning before a strong aftershock spare people some injuries.
strings.余震过后，头顶那块斜搭着的楼板裂开了一道新缝，灰土簌簌地往下漏，裂缝还在一点点变: After the aftershock, a new crack has opened in the slab lying at an angle overhead; dust sifts down and the crack is slowly widening. Someone has to crawl into the lowest corner at the very back and prop the filing cabinet up under it. Pick one person to go.
strings.你今天不是来谈合作的。你约了周敏：五十万，买她手里那个U盘——里面有何志强行贿、: You didn’t come here to talk partnership. You set up a meeting with Michelle Zhou: half a million for the USB drive in her bag — the proof of Steven Ho’s bribes and the illegally added floors. Get it, and the hundred-million south-city project belongs to your company. And you know one more thing: the original drawings for this building show only ten floors.
strings.你们这些坐办公室的，楼一晃，跑得比哪个都慢。: You office people. The building shakes and you run slower than anybody.
strings.你吃上一口，替他保密: You get a bite to eat; you keep his secret
strings.你怀孕七周了，谁也没告诉，连男朋友都还不知道。这两天你一直恶心想吐。你学过护理，: You are seven weeks pregnant and have told no one, not even your boyfriend. For two days you have been fighting nausea. You trained as a nurse — you know what severe dehydration does to the child inside you.
strings.你的保温箱里还压着一单没送出去的外卖：一份回锅肉盖饭、两瓶冰红茶（约 900 千: Your cooler box still holds one undelivered order: twice-cooked pork over rice and two bottles of iced tea (about 900 kcal, 1 L of water). After the quake you quietly shoved the box behind you and said nothing — you have a seven-year-old daughter waiting at home.
strings.你的秘密就藏不住了；可只有大家帮忙，你才躺得住: Your secret will be out; but only with everyone's help can you stay lying down
strings.你给何志强做了八年账。那两层违规加盖楼的“验收费”、逢年过节给各路人的红包，都是: You have kept Steven Ho’s books for eight years. The “inspection fees” for those two illegally added floors, the red envelopes handed round to all sorts of people at every festival — you carried them out yourself. The USB drive in your bag holds the whole ledger. It was your way out. Today Leonard Qin came to the office under the name of a partnership; in fact he came to make you a deal: half a million, for the drive. Your son’s bone-marrow transplant is short by exactly that much.
strings.保住她的嗓子和力气；可那是她妈妈: Saves her voice and strength; but that is her mother out there
strings.保住秘密，但以后被拆穿会更糟: The secret holds — but it will be worse when it comes apart
strings.保住秘密，活着出去: Keep the secret and get out alive
strings.保住肚子里的孩子：活着出去，而且身体不能垮（健康 ≥ 45）: Keep the baby: get out alive, and don’t let your body fail (health ≥ 45)
strings.偶尔闪一格: A bar flickers now and then
strings.偷出来，掰断，扔进碎砖缝里: Steal it out, snap it in half, drop it between the broken bricks
strings.儿子从医院请了假来认领遗物，抱着那个黑色公文包哭了很久。包里有一本手写的账本，和: Her son took leave from the hospital to claim her effects. He held the black briefcase and cried for a long time. Inside were a handwritten ledger and one of his own hospital bills. Where that ledger ended up, nobody can say.

strings.先把压在塌下来那头的人拖出来: First drag out whoever is under the end that dropped
strings.先把朵朵送出去，老刘交给医生: Send Daisy out first; the doctor stays with Dustin
strings.先把朵朵送出去：她最小: Send Daisy out first: she’s the youngest
strings.先把水递上去，隔着裂缝陪她说话: Pass water up first, and talk to her through the crack
strings.先把话说清楚：秦朗，你说“原来是几层”，是什么意思？: First, say it plainly. Leonard Qin, what do you mean, how many floors it was meant to have?
strings.先用皮带勒紧他的两条大腿，再撬: Strap his thighs tight with belts first, then pry
strings.先给他灌两升水，再撬: Get two litres of water into him first, then pry
strings.先给女儿打个电话，剩下的交出来: Call his daughter first, then hand over what’s left
strings.先给朵朵输上：她最小，还在发烧: Put Daisy on first: she is the youngest, and still feverish
strings.先给林小雨输上：她已经吐了好几天了: Put Lily Lin on first: she has been throwing up for days
strings.先给老刘输上，等通道打通就能解压: Dustin first, so he can be released the moment the tunnel opens
strings.先给被楼板压住腿的人输上: Put the one whose leg is pinned under the slab on first
strings.先让 {protagonist} 喝下一升半水，再撬: Have {protagonist} drink a litre and a half of water first, then pry

strings.先送手电和电池，让我们能看清楚、给你们指路: Send flashlights and batteries first, so we can see and guide you
strings.先送药和绷带，有人伤得很重: Send medicine and bandages first — someone is badly hurt
strings.先顾活人：所有人先去扒吃的、找水: The living first: everyone digs for food and water
strings.全部交出来，充进大家的手机里: Hand it all over, charge everyone’s phones
strings.全部关机，电留到救援队来了再用: Switch everything off, save the charge for when the rescuers come
strings.公平，可她和孩子扛不扛得住？: Fair — but can she and the baby hold out?
strings.公平；可她和孩子扛不扛得住，谁也不知道: Fair; whether she and the baby can hold out, nobody knows
strings.六岁的孩子钻得过一拃宽的缝；可撬的是头顶这块斜楼板，三角区会跟着晃，撬不好还会伤: A six-year-old could squeeze through a hand-span gap; but the slab overhead is what you would be prying, the triangle will shake with it, and a bad pry will hurt someone
strings.其实没什么用，可大家总得做点什么: It does no real good, but they have to do something
strings.冯建军倒退着爬出了缝口。临走前，他把头盔上的灯摘下来，塞进了离他最近的那只手里。: Jim Feng backs out through the slit. Just before he goes, he unclips the lamp from his helmet and presses it into the nearest hand.
strings.冯建军冲着缝口喊了一嗓子：“我不出去了！你们吊！”然后转过身，把离他最近的人往柱: Jim Feng shouts at the slit: “I’m not coming out! Lift it!” Then he turns and moves everyone near him back against the column.
strings.冯建军叹了口气，没再劝。: Jim Feng sighs, and does not argue any further.
strings.冯建军对着对讲机说了很久。外面的吊车熄了火，换成了电锤“突突突”的声音。: Jim Feng talks into the radio for a long time. Outside, the crane shuts down and the jackhammer starts up: thud, thud, thud.
strings.冯建军愣了一下，还是把两袋盐水剪开了口子，挨个递了过去。咸的，可没有人嫌弃。: Jim Feng hesitates, then cuts both bags open and passes them round. It is salty, and nobody complains.
strings.冯建军把头盔上的灯拧暗了一点，挨个看了看大家的脸：“快了。出去以前，我得先说件事: Jim Feng turns his helmet lamp down a notch and looks at each of their faces in turn. "Not long now. Before we go, there's something I have to say. In seventy-six, the day they dug me out, they dug my uncle out with me. He could still talk when he came out. He drank a big bowl of cold water, sat up and smoked a cigarette, and half an hour later he was gone. When you go out, nobody plays the hero and climbs out on their own, nobody gulps down cold water. Do what the doctors say."
strings.冯建军把输液袋挂在一根钢筋上，嘴里一直念叨：“没事儿，有我呢。”: Jim Feng hangs the bag on a length of rebar, muttering: “It’s all right. I’m here.”
strings.冯建军是最后一个从洞口爬出来的。他在警戒线外蹲着抽了一根烟，第二天又跟着队伍去了: Jim Feng was the last one out of the gap. He squatted outside the cordon and smoked one cigarette, and the next day he moved on with the team to the next building. Back in Tangshan a group photo went up on the wall of the repair shop; everyone in it is grey with dust, and he is the only one grinning. Every winter the people who came out of the triangle receive a box of Tangshan honey pastry.
strings.冯建军的追悼会是在唐山老家开的。来了很多人，其中有一个头发全白的老兵——就是 1: Jim Feng’s funeral was held back home in Tangshan. A great many people came, among them a white-haired veteran — the soldier who had dug him, aged nine, out of the ground in 1976. Above the funeral hall hung his yellow hard hat with the paint flaking off. The headlamp was still burning; his grandson had secretly put in a new battery.
strings.冯建军跪在老刘身边，找了三次才扎进血管。透明的盐水一滴一滴地往下走，老刘盯着它，: Jim Feng kneels beside Dustin and needs three tries to find a vein. The clear saline goes down drip by drip. Dustin stares at it for a long time.
strings.冷静、果断、有主见，看不起何志强；做事讲效率，必要时可以很冷血；只尊重有本事的人: Calm, decisive, sure of his own judgement; he has no respect for Steven Ho. Everything is about efficiency, and he can be cold-blooded when he has to be. He only respects competence.
strings.几个人凑在手机屏幕前，看着那个转个不停的圈。: Several heads together in front of the screen, watching the little circle turn.
strings.几个人把会议桌腿塞进楼板底下，喊着号子一起往下压。: Several of them jam a table leg under the slab and bear down on it together, counting the heaves out loud.
strings.几个人把桌腿插进楼板底下，喊着号子一起往下压。: Several of them jam a table leg under the slab and bear down together, counting the heaves.
strings.几个人挪到裂缝底下，把桌腿插进了缝里。: Several of them move under the crack and jam a table leg into it.
strings.几个人轮流趴在西墙根，一块一块往外抠碎砖。: They take turns lying at the foot of the west wall, prising out broken brick piece by piece.
strings.几双手在灰土里摸索着，把人一个一个拖到了还能坐直的地方。: Hands feel their way through the dust and drag people, one by one, to where they can still sit up.
strings.几条短信全都卡在“发送中”，转了一夜的圈。: Every message sticks at “Sending”, spinning all night.
strings.几条短信里，有一条在凌晨显示“已送达”。: Of the few messages, one shows “Delivered” in the small hours.
strings.几部手机剩下的电量加在一起（一部手机满电算 100%）。开手电干活、开机等信号、: The charge left in all the phones added together (one fully charged phone = 100%). Flashlights for work, a phone left on for a signal, sending texts — everything draws on this.
strings.出血一点一点少了，到天亮的时候，几乎停了。小腹那种往下坠的疼，也松开了。: The bleeding lessens little by little, and by daybreak it has almost stopped. The dragging ache in her belly lets go.
strings.出院以后，他的左前臂里多了两块钢板。他回了华城，照样跑项目、谈合作，只是每到一栋: When he came out of hospital there were two steel plates in his left forearm. He went back to Huacheng and carried on running projects and cutting deals; only now, in every new building, he goes down to the basement first to look at the load-bearing columns before he goes up to the meeting.
strings.出院前，医生关上门跟她谈了很久。那个孩子没能保住。她没有告诉任何人，连男朋友也没: Before she was discharged, the doctor shut the door and talked with her for a long time. The baby didn’t make it. She told no one, not even her boyfriend. The next year she qualified as a first responder and joined a civilian rescue team. She is first through the gap on every call-out.
strings.出院后的第三个星期，调查组在他家楼下等他。验收单的复印件摆在桌上，他看了很久，在: Three weeks after he left the hospital, the investigation team was waiting downstairs. They laid photocopies of the acceptance certificates on the table. He read them for a long time, then pressed his thumbprint onto every page. The day Hongyuan went into liquidation he walked alone to the site of Jinhua Tower and stood outside the hoarding all afternoon. Nobody recognised him.
strings.出院第二周，她在一家茶馆见了秦朗。U盘换成了一张银行卡。儿子的骨髓移植是八月做的: In her second week out of hospital she met Leonard Qin in a teahouse. The USB drive became a bank card. Her son’s transplant went ahead in August and went well. She resigned, changed her phone number, and never spoke to anyone at Hongyuan again. Only, every time she passes a teahouse, she holds her bag a little tighter.
strings.出院那天，她才告诉男朋友自己怀孕了。他愣了很久，然后蹲在病房门口哭了。孩子是冬天: The day she was discharged she finally told her boyfriend she was pregnant. He stared at her for a long time, then crouched down in the ward doorway and cried. The baby was born in winter. In the delivery room the nurse asked if she was afraid. She said, “No. I’ve been under a building.”
strings.刚爬进去十几米，{actor} 就卡在了两根管子中间。老陶骂骂咧咧地把人倒拖回检: Ten metres into the crawl, {actor} jams between two pipes. Tom hauls {actor.him} backwards to the hatch, swearing the whole way, then shoulders his sack and leaves.
strings.删掉，人都这样了: Delete it. Look at the state of us.
strings.别人怎么想随他们: Let them think what they like
strings.别出声，狗能闻到我们: Stay quiet — the dog can smell us
strings.别动他：先用文件柜把楼板垫住，等救援队来了输上液再搬: Don’t move him: shore the slab with the filing cabinet and wait for the rescuers to get an IV in before we lift
strings.别敲了，让她省点力气: Stop knocking. Let her save her strength.
strings.别睡死啊，跟我说说话。你家里几口人？: Don’t go under on me — talk to me. How many in your family?
strings.别自己吓自己：柜子撑了这么久，还会接着撑。省点力气和水: Stop scaring yourselves: the cabinet has held this long and it will go on holding. Save the strength and the water
strings.劝她别喊：喊破嗓子也传不出去，留着力气等静默搜听: Tell her not to shout: she can scream her throat out and it won’t carry — save it for the silence-and-listen
strings.勒住以后，腿里的毒素冲不进全身，命多半能保住，腿多半保不住: With the belts on, the toxins in the legs can’t reach the rest of the body. The life is likely saved; the legs most likely are not
strings.包里是一个U盘和一本手写的账本，一页一页记着“验收费”“过节费”，日期、金额、经: Inside the bag are a USB drive and a handwritten ledger, page after page of “inspection fees” and “holiday gifts”, with dates, amounts and the name of whoever handled them.
strings.医生给老刘挂上盐水的时候，朵朵已经被托出了洞口。剩下的人一个接一个跟了出去，最后: By the time the doctor has the IV into Dustin, Daisy is already out of the gap. The rest follow one by one; Dustin is last, an IV line in his arm, squinting up at the daylight.
strings.十二层的写字楼塌了。你们挤在三楼一个一米二高的夹缝里，外面的人还不知道这里有活人: A twelve-story office tower has come down. You are wedged into a gap on the third floor barely 1.2 metres high, and no one outside knows anyone is alive in here.
strings.十二月底，她生下一个男孩，小名叫“石头”。三角区里出来的人凑钱给孩子打了一把小银: At the end of December she gave birth to a boy; they called him Shitou — Little Stone. The people who came out of the triangle pooled money for a little silver lock engraved with Safe and Well. The next year she passed the exam into the emergency department of the city’s No. 1 Hospital. On her first night shift she took in a worker who had come off a scaffold.
strings.半夜，{actor} 听见黄勇那边有塑料袋窸窸窣窣的声音，空气里飘过来一丝饭菜的: In the middle of the night, {actor} hears plastic rustling near Ken Huang, and a trace of cooked food drifts through the air — the delivery cooler box.
strings.半夜，东头传来一声闷响，像有人一脚踩扁了一只铁桶——那个文件柜折了。楼板往下一坐: In the middle of the night there is a dull bang from the east end, like someone stamping flat an oil drum. The filing cabinet has folded. The slab drops, dust pours down on everyone, and the whole triangle is coughing.
strings.半瓶矿泉水: Half a bottle of mineral water
strings.华城装饰的项目总监，宏远在城南项目上的竞争对手，今天下午说是来“谈合作”。在部队: Project director at Huacheng Decoration, Hongyuan’s rival on the south-city job; this afternoon he said he had come to “talk partnership”. Eight years a combat engineer in the army. He was tapping walls and reading cracks from the moment he got into the triangle. His left forearm is broken.
strings.压了才几个小时，挤压综合征的风险还不算大；撬板子会让头顶晃一晃: Only a few hours pinned — crush syndrome is not yet the main danger; prying the slab will shake the ceiling
strings.压低声音：东西你拿走，出去以后告诉救援队我们在这儿: Keep your voice down: take what you like, but when you’re out tell the rescuers we’re here
strings.压得越久越危险；输上液，等救援队来了再解压: The longer the compression, the worse the danger; get fluids in, and release it when the rescuers are ready
strings.压得越久，搬开那一刻越危险：可能当场心脏骤停，也可能几个小时后突然不行: The longer the compression, the more dangerous the lift: the heart may stop on the spot, or give out hours later
strings.压得越久，撬开的那一刻越危险: The longer the compression, the more dangerous the moment it is lifted
strings.原型：2008 年 5 月 12 日汶川 8.0 级地震。很多幸存者在废墟下坚持: Inspired by the magnitude-8.0 Wenchuan earthquake of May 12, 2008. Many survivors held out under the rubble for more than 100 hours before they were dug out: some kept going by drinking their own urine; some took turns sleeping with the people beside them, telling each other stories, forcing themselves not to drift off for good. Some could still talk when they were pulled free, then died suddenly a few hours later of “crush syndrome”: when a limb that has been pinned for a long time is suddenly released, potassium and myoglobin from the dead muscle flood the bloodstream, causing hyperkalemia, cardiac arrest and acute kidney failure. Since then, “fluids first, then lift” has been standard practice in earthquake rescue. The first 72 hours are called the “golden window”, after which the odds of rescue fall steeply — yet in the 2023 Turkey–Syria earthquake, people were still pulled out alive after more than 200 hours under the rubble. Search dogs, life detectors, the “silent listening” periods at rescue sites, and the rule that tapping costs less strength than shouting are all real search-and-rescue practice.
strings.又一个分不清白天黑夜的时辰。有人提议：轮流睡，轮流说话——谁也别睡死过去。: Another stretch of hours with no day and no night in it. Someone suggests: sleep in turns, talk in turns — nobody slides away in their sleep.
strings.又一块碎板滑了下来。缝没撬开，{actor} 的手先肿了。: Another broken slab slides down. The crack doesn’t open, and {actor}’s hand swells up.
strings.又一次余震。三角区咯吱作响，灰土簌簌地往下掉，所有人抱着头缩成一团。等摇晃停下来: Another aftershock. The triangle creaks, dust and grit sift down, and everyone curls up with their arms over their heads. When the shaking stops, the crack overhead looks a little wider.
strings.反问秦朗：一个外人，今天到底来我们公司干什么？: Turn it back on Leonard Qin: what is an outsider doing in our office today?
strings.叔叔，出去了我想喝冰的可乐，一大瓶。: Mister, when we get out I want a cold Coke. A big bottle.
strings.只有瘦小的人挤得过去；你会丢下所有人，也可能把救援队带回来: Only a small, thin person can squeeze through; you would be leaving everyone behind — and you might bring the rescuers back
strings.可楼板只往下沉了两指，就停住了——旁边那个木垛吃住了劲，木板被压得吱吱叫，一根也: But the slab drops only two fingers' width and stops. The crib beside it has taken the load; the planks groan under it, and not one of them breaks.
strings.可能冤枉好人: An innocent person may be blamed
strings.可能有人会咳出肺炎: Someone may cough their way into pneumonia
strings.吊装时落下的碎块砸伤: Struck by debris during the lift
strings.吊车刚一起吊，头顶就“咔”地响了一声。冯建军一下子扑了过去，护住了离他最近的人。: The moment the crane takes the weight there is a crack overhead. Jim Feng throws himself across the person nearest him. When the debris comes down, he doesn’t make a sound.
strings.吊车起吊的时候，头顶落下一片碎块，砸在 {actor} 身上。: As the crane takes the weight, debris comes down from overhead and lands on {actor}.
strings.后半夜，{actor} 的手突然垂了下去。有人扑上去按胸口，按了很久很久。: Late in the night, {actor}’s hand suddenly drops. Someone throws herself onto {actor.his} chest and presses, for a long, long time.
strings.后半夜，老刘的手突然垂了下去。有人扑上去按他的胸口，按了很久很久。: Late in the night, Dustin’s hand suddenly drops. Someone throws herself on his chest and presses, for a long, long time.
strings.后半夜，血突然多了起来，又慢慢止住了。林小雨自己清楚发生了什么。她用会议纪要把自: In the small hours the bleeding suddenly gets heavier, and then slowly stops. Lily Lin knows exactly what has happened. She cleans herself up with sheets of the meeting minutes and does not say a word.
strings.后来大家才知道：救援队先从另一侧挖到了陈阿姨。她被抬出来的时候拽着队员的袖子说—: Only later did they learn: the rescuers reached Auntie Chen first, from the other side. As they lifted her out she clutched a rescuer’s sleeve and said, “There are people on the other side of that wall! Several of them!”
strings.后来，救援指挥部的值班记录里有这么一行：“凌晨，一名男子报告锦华大厦三楼东侧有幸: Later, the rescue command post log carried this line: “Small hours — a man reported survivors on the east side of the third floor, Jinhua Tower. Did not leave a name.” No one could confirm it was Tom. Three months afterwards the police raided a scrap yard on the edge of the city and seized a batch of phones and laptops stolen from the quake zone. The owner said the seller was a thin man with a northern Sichuan accent.
strings.后来，那个开挖掘机的司机上了电视。他说那天他已经抓起了一块楼板，铲斗举在半空，对: The excavator driver was on television afterwards. He said he already had a slab in the bucket that day, raised in the air, when the radio suddenly shouted stop. He said his hands had never shaken like that in his life. Those carried out alive: {survivors}. Those who did not live to see it: {dead}.
strings.听一听家里人的声音；家里人也许会去找救援队: Hear a voice from home; and family may go looking for the rescue teams
strings.听他的：一个一个躺上担架出去，先挂上盐水再说话: Do as he says: out one at a time on stretchers, drip first, talking later
strings.听救援队的安排: Do it the way the rescue team says
strings.听秦朗的：拆了会议桌，在柜子旁边码一个“井”字形的木垛，替它分担: Do as Leonard Qin says: break up the conference table and stack a criss-cross crib of timber beside the cabinet to share the load
strings.吴老师的包里也许有水、吃的和手机；可这是让一个六岁的孩子去翻她老师的身体: Teacher Wu’s bag may hold water, food and a phone — but this means sending a six-year-old to search her teacher’s body
strings.吴老师的手好凉……她是不是睡着了？: Teacher Wu’s hand is so cold… is she asleep?
strings.告诉大家，但先等等，看救援队来不来: Tell them, but wait and see if the rescue team comes
strings.告诉大家，请他们让自己躺着、多分一口水: Tell everyone, and ask to lie still and have a little more water
strings.告诉大家，马上开始往东墙挖: Tell everyone, and start digging at the east wall now
strings.告诉她我们也被困着，帮不了她: Tell her you are trapped too and cannot help
strings.告诉她：我们自己也没有水了: Tell her: we have no water ourselves
strings.周敏只说了一句：“何总，我儿子等不起‘出去以后’。”: Michelle Zhou says only: “Mr Ho, my son can’t wait for ‘once we’re out’.”
strings.周敏愣了一下，抱包的手松了一点。: Michelle Zhou freezes for a moment, and her grip on the bag loosens a little.
strings.周敏把包往怀里又抱紧了一点。: Michelle Zhou hugs the bag a little tighter.
strings.周敏摸黑把U盘塞进了秦朗手里。秦朗在一张会议纪要的背面写了一张欠条。: Michelle Zhou feels for the drive in the dark and presses it into Leonard Qin’s hand. Leonard Qin writes an IOU on the back of a sheet of meeting notes.
strings.周敏沉默了很久，最后当着他的面，把U盘掰成了两截。: Michelle Zhou is quiet for a long time, and then, in front of him, snaps the drive in two.
strings.周敏没说话，过了很久，黑暗里传来拉链的声音。: Michelle Zhou says nothing. After a long time, the sound of a zip comes out of the dark.
strings.周敏猛地醒了，一把攥住了 {actor} 伸进她包里的手。: Michelle Zhou wakes with a jolt and seizes {actor}’s hand inside her bag.
strings.周敏醒了，一把攥住了何志强伸进她包里的手。“何总，”她一字一句地说，“你想干什么: Michelle Zhou wakes and seizes Steven Ho’s hand inside her bag. “Mr Ho,” she says, word by word, “what do you think you’re doing?”
strings.咬住袖子，一个人缩在角落里熬过去: Bite down on a sleeve and ride it out alone in the corner
strings.咬牙忍着，等救援队来: Grit your teeth and wait for the rescue team
strings.唐山口音，爱说“没事儿，有我呢”“咱慢慢来”。: A Tangshan accent. He likes to say, “It’s all right, I’m here,” and “We’ll take it slow.”
strings.喊得越响越好；嗓子和身体里的水，都要搭进去: The louder the better; it costs your voice and the water in your body
strings.嘴里能湿一湿，可尿里的盐还得靠身体里的水排出去；会恶心，也伤肾: It wets the mouth, but the salts in it still have to be flushed out with the body's own water; it's nauseating and hard on the kidneys
strings.嘿嘿，各位老板莫紧张，我就是个捡破烂的。: Heh heh. No need to get nervous, bosses. I just pick up junk.
strings.在会议纪要背面写几句话，折好塞进口袋: Write a few lines on the back of the meeting notes and fold them into a pocket
strings.在压塌的办公桌和柜子里摸索：零食、半瓶水、药、充电宝，也可能只摸到一手碎玻璃。越: Feel through the crushed desks and cabinets: snacks, half a bottle of water, pills, a power bank — or nothing but a handful of broken glass. There is less to find as the days go by. A flashlight makes a more careful search possible.
strings.在它的项圈上缠一张纸条：楼名、楼层、几个人，把它推出去: Tape a note to his collar — tower name, floor, how many people — and push him out
strings.在管道井的一个拐角，{actor} 被卡住了，胸口挤在两根管子中间，喘不上气。老: At a bend in the pipe shaft, {actor} jams, chest squeezed between two pipes, unable to breathe. Tom pulls from the front for a long time, and then can’t pull any more.
strings.在管道井的一个拐角，{actor} 被卡住了，进退不得。老陶在前面拽、后面推，折: At a bend in the pipe shaft, {actor} jams fast, unable to go forward or back. Tom hauls from the front and shoves from behind for more than an hour before dragging {actor.him} back out to the hatch.
strings.地震时正好来三楼会议室送下午茶。瘦，手脚麻利，常年风里雨里跑单。腰上挂着跑单用的: He happened to be on the third floor delivering afternoon tea when the quake hit. Thin, quick, out in every kind of weather. A big power bank for his delivery app hangs at his waist. He’s from Dazhou, same as Dustin the guard downstairs; they smoke together every day.
strings.坐到他身边，什么也不问: Sit down beside him and ask nothing
strings.城南项目的招标结果出来，华城中标了。庆功宴上秦朗只喝了一杯茶，提前走了。那个U盘: When the tender result for the south-city project came out, Huacheng had won. At the celebration dinner Leonard Qin drank one cup of tea and left early. He never handed the drive over and never used it — it lay in the bottom drawer of his desk, next to an IOU written on the back of the meeting notes.
strings.塌方扬起的水泥粉尘，会慢慢沉降；余震和挖掘会让它重新扬起来。: Cement dust thrown up by the collapse. It settles slowly; aftershocks and digging stir it up again.
strings.墙角那桶 18.9 升的桶装水被倒下的文件柜和一堆碎砖压着，要把碎块一点点扒开，: The 18.9 L water jug in the corner is pinned under the toppled filing cabinet and a heap of broken brick. The rubble has to be cleared bit by bit, then the cabinet pried up.
strings.墙角那桶 18.9 升的桶装水被倒下的文件柜和碎砖压着。要把碎块一点点扒开、把柜: The 18.9 L water-cooler jug in the corner is pinned under a toppled filing cabinet and a heap of broken brick. Someone will have to pick the rubble away piece by piece and pry the cabinet up. Heavy work; in the dark it goes slowly and glass cuts are easy; shifting the cabinet shakes the structure overhead. The water dispenser lying beside it may still hold a little water.
strings.墙那边传来很轻的敲击声，接着是一个女人沙哑的声音：“有人吗……我是做保洁的陈阿姨: Through the wall comes a very faint tapping, then a woman’s hoarse voice: “Is anyone there… I’m Auntie Chen, I do the cleaning… my leg is stuck, I can’t get out…”
strings.墙那边传来陈阿姨断断续续的声音：“我闺女……下个月十八号结婚。要是我出不去，你们: Auntie Chen's voice comes through the wall in pieces. "My daughter... is getting married on the eighteenth of next month. If I don't get out, tell her for me: the money I saved for her is in the tin box under my bed back home. And... don't hire the wedding dress. Buy one." Then she gives a little laugh. "Can you remember all that?"
strings.墙那边很久没说话，最后轻轻“嗯”了一声。: For a long time there is no answer. Then, softly: "Mm."
strings.墙那边沉默了很久，最后说：“晓得了。不怪你们。”: There is a long silence on the other side. Then: "I understand. I don't blame you."
strings.墙那边沉默了很久，最后轻轻说了一声：“晓得了。你们保重。”: The other side of the wall is silent for a long time. Then, softly: “I hear you. Look after yourselves.”
strings.墙那边，陈阿姨的声音一天比一天哑：“有没有……一口水……我嘴里全是灰……”有人摸: From the other side of the wall Auntie Chen's voice grows hoarser by the day. "Is there... a mouthful of water... my mouth is full of dust..." Someone feels along the foot of the wall: between two slabs there is a gap just wide enough to push a thin tube through.
strings.声音很轻，常说“对不起”“没事的”；一讲到伤病，口气就变得很干脆。: A very quiet voice; she says “sorry” and “it’s okay” a lot. The moment the talk turns to injuries, her tone goes crisp.
strings.外卖平台把他的骑手账号换成了黑白头像。他女儿七岁生日那天，站长带着十几个骑手去了: The delivery platform turned his rider avatar black and white. On the day his daughter turned seven the station manager took a dozen riders to his home, each of them carrying a cake. The little girl counted them one by one, and at the end she asked, “Where’s my dad’s?”
strings.外部救援力量抵达这片街区的进度。: How close the outside rescue forces are to reaching this district.
strings.外面传来哨声和喊声：救援队员全部撤出了刚挖开的通道，等余震过去才敢再进来。: Whistles and shouting outside: the rescue crew has pulled back out of the tunnel they just cut. They won’t come in again until the aftershock has passed.
strings.外面安静了好几秒。然后有人扯着嗓子喊：“有人！下面有人！叫救援队过来——机器都别: Outside, several seconds of silence. Then someone bellows: "Someone's alive! There's someone down there! Get the rescue team, and nobody touch the machines!"
strings.外面扩音器的喊声里，忽然夹进来一个女人嘶哑的声音：“朵朵——唐朵朵——妈妈在这儿: Into the megaphone voice outside cuts a woman’s hoarse shout: “Daisy — Daisy Tang — Mama’s here —” Daisy’s voice goes shrill at once: “That’s my mama! That’s my mama!” The one nearest her is {actor}.
strings.外面的人一刻都没停，我听得见。: They haven’t stopped out there. I can hear them.
strings.外面的人听了一会儿，什么也没听见。发动机又轰地响了起来。: The people outside listen for a while and hear nothing. The engine roars back into life.
strings.外面的人是不是在找我们？他们晓得我叫啥子名字不？: Are the people outside looking for us? Do they know my name?
strings.外面的人知道这里有活人的程度。敲击、呼喊、短信都会增加它，时间一长会慢慢淡掉。: How sure the people outside are that someone is alive in here. Tapping, shouting and texts all raise it; it slowly fades over time.
strings.外面的医生一听说有人被压住了，隔着缝连喊了三遍：“千万别自己搬！等我们进去先给他: The moment a doctor outside heard that someone was pinned, he shouted three times through the gap: “Nobody move him! Wait until we get in and start fluids first!”
strings.外面的吊车要把压在通道口上的那块大楼板吊开。哨子一声比一声急：“冯建军！撤出来！: The crane outside is going to lift the big slab off the mouth of the tunnel. The whistles get more urgent: “Jim Feng! Get out! It may come down when we lift!” Jim Feng looks at you and doesn’t move: “If I go out now I can’t come back in until the lift is done. That’s hours.”
strings.外面的机器声越来越远，最后听不见了。有人喃喃地说：“他们是不是以为这栋楼没人了…: The sound of the machines outside gets further and further away, and then stops. Someone murmurs, “Do they think there’s no one left in this building… and they’ve gone to another one?”
strings.外面那些人先挖的是对面那栋，你们这栋排在后头。: The crews outside are digging at the block across the street first. Yours is further down the list.
strings.多一个有力气、懂塌房子的人；也多一张嘴，多一双盯着大家东西的眼睛: One more pair of strong hands that understands collapsed buildings — and one more mouth, and one more pair of eyes on everyone’s things
strings.多一条自救的路，可挖洞会让三角区更不稳: One more way out you make yourselves — but a hole will make the triangle less stable
strings.多在不稳的废墟里待两个小时: Two more hours inside an unstable ruin
strings.夜里湿着衣服会冷得发抖: Wet clothes mean shivering all night
strings.大人的嗓门传得更远；你自己要多耗不少水和力气: An adult voice carries further; it costs you a lot of water and strength
strings.大名刘德顺，在锦华大厦干了十一年保安。地震时正上楼来通知会议室的人挪车。两条小腿: Real name Dustin Liu; eleven years a guard at Jinhua Tower. He was on his way up to tell the meeting to move their cars when the quake hit. Both shins are pinned under a slab. He is still conscious.
strings.大名唐朵朵，附近小学一年级的学生，中午在四楼的“小太阳”午托班吃饭、睡午觉。那天: Her full name is Daisy Tang. A first-grader at the primary school nearby; at midday she eats and naps at the “Little Sun” after-school center on the fourth floor. That morning she had a fever and stayed off class, so Teacher Wu at the center put her down on a cot to sleep until her mother finished work at three. When the quake hit, Teacher Wu scooped her up and ran for the stairs, and the building came down. Daisy is wedged in the gap above the slanted slab over the triangle; Teacher Wu is right beside her and has not made a sound since.
strings.大家一起把手边能顶的东西全塞进去: Everyone shoves whatever they can find in under the slab
strings.大家七手八脚地按住水桶。: Everyone puts their hands to the jug at once, all thumbs.
strings.大家也许会多照顾你，也许会觉得你是个负担: They may take more care of you — or decide you are a burden
strings.大家先扶着 {protagonist} 一口一口喝完了水，又等了一个多小时，才把: They hold {protagonist} up and get the water down mouthful by mouthful, then wait more than an hour before jamming the table leg under the slab.
strings.大家先扶着老刘喝了整整两升水，又等了一个多小时，才把桌腿插进楼板底下。: They hold Dustin up while he drinks two full litres, then wait more than an hour before jamming the table leg under the slab.
strings.大家决定了：明天推选一个人，从楼梯间爬出去。: They decide: tomorrow one of them will be chosen to crawl out through the stairwell.
strings.大家又一次把桌腿插进了那道缝。: Once again they jam the table leg into the crack.
strings.大家围着老刘，你一句我一句。: They gather round Dustin and talk, one over the other.
strings.大家围着老刘，你一句我一句地跟他说话。: They gather round Dustin and talk to him, one over the other.
strings.大家屏住呼吸，听着头顶的动静。: Everyone holds their breath and listens to what is happening overhead.
strings.大家托着 {protagonist} 的头，一小口一小口地喂水。: They hold {protagonist}’s head and feed water in, one small mouthful at a time.
strings.大家把一个铁皮文件柜塞到了楼板下面，板子不再往下沉了。老刘喘着粗气说：“要得，要: They wedge a steel filing cabinet under the slab and it stops settling. Dustin, breathing hard, says, “All right. All right… I’ll wait.”
strings.大家把所有的外套都盖在了 {protagonist} 身上。: They pile every jacket they have over {protagonist}.
strings.大家把所有的外套都盖在老刘身上。: Everyone piles their jackets on Dustin.
strings.大家把手机交到一起，谁干活谁拿着照亮，其余的全部关机。: Everyone pools their phones; whoever is working carries the light, and the rest stay off.
strings.大家把钢管、饭盒、手机都攥在手里，竖着耳朵等发动机熄火的那一刻。: They hold the steel pipe, the lunch tins and the phones ready, ears straining for the moment the engine cuts out.
strings.大家挪开了一点，给她留出了一小块地方。: They shift back a little and leave her a small space of her own.
strings.大家点了头。冯建军拍了拍离他最近的那个肩膀：“好。咱慢慢来。”: They nod. Jim Feng pats the nearest shoulder. "Good. We take it slow."
strings.大家知道有这条路，什么时候挖再说: They know the way is there; when to dig can wait
strings.大家竖着耳朵听，谁也没出声。机器声时近时远。: Everyone listens hard. Nobody makes a sound. The machines fade in and out.
strings.大家轮流跟老刘说话，说了一整夜。天亮的时候，他已经有力气骂人了：“你们几个，吵得: They take turns talking to Dustin all night. By dawn he has strength enough to swear at them: “You lot. Keeping a man awake with all that noise.”
strings.大家轮流躺在裂缝底下，张着嘴接那一滴一滴的雨水，水里有一股水泥味。: They take turns lying under the crack with their mouths open to the dripping, and the water tastes of cement.
strings.大家都知道你有: They all know you have it
strings.大家都闭上嘴，用鼻子小口小口地喘气。: Everyone shuts their mouth and breathes in small sips through the nose.
strings.大家隔着裂缝，一句一句地教她：“摸到包没有？拉链在哪边？”: Through the crack they talk her through it, phrase by phrase: “Can you feel the bag? Which side is the zip on?”
strings.大雨砸在废墟上哗哗作响，外面的机器声和喊声全被盖住了，地上开始积水。: Heavy rain hammers on the rubble, drowning out the machines and voices outside. Water begins to pool on the floor.
strings.大雨顺着裂缝灌进来，地上积了一层泥水。所有人的衣服都湿透了，冷得牙齿直打颤。: Heavy rain pours in through the cracks and muddy water pools on the floor. Everyone is soaked through, shivering so hard their teeth chatter.
strings.天快亮的时候，{actor} 迷迷糊糊睁开眼，看见老陶背起了蛇皮袋，正一点一点往: Towards dawn, {actor} comes half awake and sees Tom shouldering the sack and edging toward the hatch. The sack is bulging, and the neck of a water bottle shows at the top. He looks back at {actor} and puts a finger to his lips.
strings.天快亮的时候，林小雨蜷在角落里，很久很久都没有出声。: Towards dawn Lily Lin is curled up in a corner, and for a long, long time she makes no sound.
strings.太累了，让别人敲吧: Too tired — let someone else knock
strings.头顶的混凝土被切开了一个脸盆大的洞，一束强光照了进来：“下面的人别动！我们一个一: A hole the size of a washbasin has been cut in the concrete overhead, and a hard beam of light comes down: “Nobody down there move! We’ll bring you out one at a time!” The passage is narrow — one person at a time, nearly an hour each — and another aftershock could hit at any moment. Who goes first?
strings.奶声奶气的四川话，爱问“为啥子”，常说“我不哭了，我勇敢”。: A small, babyish Sichuan accent. She loves asking “why”, and says, “I’m not crying any more. I’m brave.”
strings.她发着烧，嗓子已经哑了: She is feverish, and her voice is already going
strings.她口袋里那张纸是写给儿子的，字迹工工整整，像一张报销单：存折在哪、密码多少、医保: The paper in her pocket was a letter to her son, written as neatly as an expense claim: where the passbook is, what the code is, how to claim on the medical insurance, the number for the marrow registry. The last line read: “Mama has never done a single thing to wrong you.” Under it she had drawn two lines.
strings.她可以不干活；水，一视同仁: She can stop working; the water stays equal
strings.她就成了要分水的一张嘴；裂缝不用动: She becomes one more mouth to share water with; the crack doesn’t have to be touched
strings.她是从管道井里钻出来的。在救护车上，她死死抓着护士的手，第一句话是：“我怀孕了，: She came out through the pipe shaft. In the ambulance she gripped the nurse’s hand and said, first: “I’m pregnant. Seven weeks.” Then: “Third floor, east side — there are still people.” The baby survived. She often said afterwards that in that shaft she talked to her child the whole way up.
strings.她是学护理的，知道自己缺的是什么: She trained as a nurse; she knows what her body is missing
strings.她现在最缺的就是水: Water is what she needs most now
strings.她的护士资格证一直夹在包的内袋里，塑封皮被压出了一道裂痕。她手机相册里的最后一张: Her nurse’s licence stayed in the inside pocket of her bag, the laminate split across. The last photo in her phone was of a crack in the pantry wall, taken last month.
strings.她能撑下去；可每一班都要从水里匀出一口，谁也说不准还要熬多久: She can hold on; but a mouthful goes from the water every shift, and nobody knows how long this will last
strings.她要的就是有人记得: All she wants is for someone to remember
strings.她那张纸写给一个还没有名字的孩子：“对不起，妈妈没能带你看看外面。外面其实挺好的: Her letter was to a child who never got a name: “I’m sorry, Mama couldn’t show you the outside. The outside is really not bad. There’s sun.” On the back, in a nurse’s small hand: “Seven weeks pregnant. If I still have a pulse when you find me, please tell the doctor.”
strings.字写得歪歪扭扭；写完心里会静一点，也可能更难受: The writing comes out crooked; it settles you a little — or hurts more
strings.孩子先走，天经地义；大人们在黑暗里多等一个钟头: The child goes first, as it should be; the adults wait one more hour in the dark
strings.孩子先走；里面腾出地方，医生好给老刘解压: The child goes first; and with the space cleared, the doctor can release Dustin
strings.孩子是腊月里出生的，七斤二两。护士抱给她看的时候，她第一句话是：“那时候他才七周: The baby was born in the depths of winter, three and a half kilos. When the nurse brought him to her, the first thing she said was: "He was seven weeks then." Everyone who came out of the triangle received a one-month photograph, and on the back: thank you for those mouthfuls of water.
strings.孩子的声音尖，最容易被认出来；可她发着烧，嗓子已经哑了: A child’s voice carries, and it is the easiest to recognise; but she has a fever and her throat is already raw
strings.孩子脱水比大人快得多: A child dehydrates far faster than an adult
strings.守着伤员和水桶，听着外面的动静: Watch over the injured and the water, and listen for what’s happening outside
strings.宏远装饰的老板，公司租下了锦华大厦整个三楼。地震时正在会议室给大家开会。西装革履: Owner of Hongyuan Decoration, which leases the entire third floor of Jinhua Tower. He was holding a meeting in the conference room when the quake hit. Suit and tie; a shard of glass has opened a gash across his forehead. Used to giving orders.
strings.小黄，你屋头幺妹儿几岁了？七岁？好，好。: Ken — your girl at home, how old is she now? Seven? Good. That’s good.
strings.就在最后一个人被托出去之前，又一次余震。等救援队员重新钻进去，{actor} 已: Just before the last person was lifted out, another aftershock. When the rescuers got back in, {actor} was not breathing.
strings.就守在洞口轮流敲、轮流喊: Stay at the gap, taking turns to knock and shout
strings.川东口音，说话慢。: Eastern Sichuan accent. He talks slowly.
strings.川北口音，说话前先“嘿嘿”一笑：“各位老板莫紧张，我就是个捡破烂的。”: A northern Sichuan accent; he gives a little “heh heh” before he speaks: “No need to get nervous, bosses. I just pick up junk.”
strings.干活时开手电，其余时间全部关机: Flashlights while working, everything else switched off
strings.开着的那部手机突然连震了几下——一条求救短信终于发了出去，还收到一条回复：“已转: The phone left on suddenly buzzed several times — a distress text had finally gone through, and a reply came back: “Forwarded to the rescue command post. Hold on!”
strings.当众问她包里到底装了什么: Ask her, in front of everyone, what is in the bag
strings.当场揭穿: Call it out on the spot
strings.当着所有人的面说出来: Say it out loud, in front of everyone
strings.往西边挖，往有机器声的地方挖: Dig west, towards the sound of the machines
strings.忍着，少说话少动: Endure it; talk less, move less
strings.怕黑、怕一个人待着；哭累了就睡，醒了就问妈妈什么时候来。大人跟她说话的时候，她会: Afraid of the dark and of being left alone. She cries herself to sleep, and when she wakes she asks when her mother is coming. When adults talk to her she tries hard to be brave, and sometimes comforts them instead.
strings.慢一点；可出去的那一刻，往往最危险: Slower; but the moment of coming out is often the most dangerous
strings.憨厚、能忍，疼得满头大汗也只说“莫得事”；总惦记着楼里的人有没有跑出去。: Good-natured, long-suffering; sweat pouring off him with the pain and still saying “it’s nothing.” He keeps asking whether everyone else in the building got out.
strings.我们自己都快撑不住了；可她一个人在上面，能撑多久？: We can barely hold on ourselves; and she is up there alone — how long can she last?
strings.我们陪着老刘，等他一起出去: We stay with Dustin and come out together
strings.我会数到一百了！一、二、三、四……: I can count to a hundred! One, two, three, four…
strings.我侄儿在九楼上班……九楼。: My nephew works on the ninth floor… the ninth floor.
strings.我在这楼干了十一年，哪根柱子是歪的我都晓得。: Eleven years I worked in this building. I know which column leans.
strings.我妈妈说三点钟来接我。现在几点了？: My mum said she’d come at three. What time is it now?
strings.我把自己的那份分一点给她: I’ll give her some of my own share
strings.所有人一起喊，上面的狗也跟着叫了起来。: Everyone shouts at once, and the dog above starts barking with them.
strings.所有人一起喊：“这里有人！”: Everyone shouts together: “There are people here!”
strings.所有人一起敲：三下一停，一直敲: Everyone knocks together: three, pause, keep going
strings.所有人一起敲：三下，停，再三下: Everyone knocks together: three, pause, three
strings.所有人在黑暗里摸索着扒抽屉、翻柜子。老刘一个人躺在那块楼板底下，没再出声。: Everyone gropes through the dark, pulling out drawers and ransacking cabinets. Dustin lies alone under the slab, and doesn’t make another sound.
strings.所有人对着裂缝一起喊，喊到嗓子劈了。: They all shout into the crack together until their voices crack.
strings.所有人扯着嗓子一起喊，喊到嗓子劈了，喊到咳出血丝。: Everyone screams until their voices crack, until they are coughing up threads of blood.
strings.所有人抱着头一动不动，听着头顶的楼板一点一点地“吱吱”作响，直到它不再响了。: Everyone freezes with their arms over their heads, listening to the slab creak, a little at a time, until it stops.
strings.所有人的目光最后都落在了 {actor} 身上。{actor} 涨红了脸：“不是: Every eye ends up on {actor}. {actor} flushes red: “It wasn’t me!”
strings.所有人轮流敲，一刻也别停: Everyone takes turns knocking, and never stops
strings.所有人轮流趴在桶口，大口大口地喝，喝到肚子发胀。: They take turns at the mouth of the jug, gulping it down until their bellies are tight.
strings.所有手机都关了。三角区里黑得伸手不见五指，只听得见彼此的呼吸。: Every phone goes off. The triangle is black as pitch; all anyone can hear is the others breathing.
strings.所有能挪的人都挪到西头去，离那个柜子远一点: Everyone who can move shifts to the west end, away from that cabinet
strings.所有能爬的人一起钻出去: Everyone who can crawl goes out together
strings.手机电量 +45；有信号的话也许能打通: Phone charge +45; if there’s a signal, maybe the call will go through
strings.手机电量是所有人共用的：开手电干活（效率高、少受伤）、留一部手机开机等信号、主动: Phone charge is shared by everyone: flashlights for work (faster, fewer injuries), one phone left on to wait for a signal, and holding phones up to send texts all compete for it. Over the days after the quake, emergency communication trucks and tower repairs bring the signal back bit by bit.
strings.扯着嗓子朝裂缝外面喊。人声比敲击更容易让外面确认“下面有活人”，但喊一阵就口干舌: Shout yourself hoarse at the crack. A human voice convinces people outside that there is someone alive down here more surely than tapping does, but a few minutes of it leaves your throat dry, burns water and strength, and pulls more dust into your lungs.
strings.把U盘给他，让他写一张欠条: Give him the drive and make him write an IOU
strings.把会议桌腿、文件柜、椅子垫到楼板下面，顶住最危险的几处裂缝，提高三角区的完好度（: Wedge table legs, the filing cabinet and chairs under the slab, propping the worst cracks, and raise the triangle’s integrity (structural stability). It means moving heavy things, and you can be crushed doing it; in the dark the work goes worse. Office furniture can only do so much — above 80 integrity there is nothing left worth shoring.
strings.把信号让给最想打电话的人: Give the signal to whoever most needs to call
strings.把所有手机的电凑到一部上，贴着裂缝一遍遍发短信：三楼东侧有活人: Pool every phone's charge into one and keep sending texts from the crack: people alive, third floor, east side
strings.把手机电筒伸到裂缝口，一闪一闪地照: Push a phone torch into the crack and flash it
strings.把手机贴着裂缝举高，一点点挪位置找信号，把楼名、楼层、人数编成短信一遍遍重发。很: Hold the phone high against the crack and edge it around looking for bars, sending the same text over and over — building name, floor, number of people. It drains the battery hard (about 6% a try), and whether it gets out depends on how far the network repairs have come.
strings.把文件夹卷成管子，每一班都往那边送一口水: Roll a folder into a tube and send a mouthful through every shift
strings.把水倒进所有能找到的瓶子和杯子里: Pour the water into every bottle and cup they can find
strings.把水给 {protagonist} 灌下去，能喝多少喝多少: Pour water into {protagonist}, as much as {protagonist.he} can drink
strings.把水给他灌下去，能喝多少喝多少: Pour water into him, as much as he can drink
strings.把汗湿的衣服从裂缝里塞出去: Push a sweat-soaked shirt out through the crack
strings.把自己的那口水给她: Give her your own mouthful of water
strings.把裂缝堵上，别让大家淋湿: Plug the crack so no one gets soaked
strings.把裂缝撬宽，现在就把她接下来: Widen the crack and lift her down now
strings.抓住身边人的手，跟着他数呼吸: Take the hand of whoever is nearest and breathe with them, counting
strings.抓紧时间睡一会: Grab some sleep while there’s time
strings.护理专业毕业，没考上医院的编制，来宏远做行政实习刚三个月。个子小，穿着一条薄连衣: A nursing graduate who didn’t make it into a hospital post; three months into an administrative internship at Hongyuan. Small, in a thin dress. She knows first aid, and from the moment she crawled into the triangle she has been checking everyone’s injuries.
strings.抱住头，等它过去: Cover your heads and wait for it to pass
strings.抽屉里的几包饼干和坚果: A few packets of biscuits and nuts from a drawer
strings.抽屉里翻出来的饼干、坚果、巧克力和半袋面包，按热量计。: Biscuits, nuts, chocolate and half a bag of bread from the desk drawers, counted in calories.
strings.拨了几次，都是“无法接通”。老陶把手机贴在胸口，再也没拿出来过。: Several tries, and every time: cannot be connected. Tom presses the phone to his chest and never takes it out again.
strings.拼命去推头顶的楼板: Shove at the slab overhead with everything you have
strings.拼命喊：“下面有人！”: Shout with everything you have: "There's someone down here!"
strings.拼命敲，一刻也不停: Knock for all you’re worth, without stopping
strings.拼尽全力喊“这里有人！”: Shout “There are people here!” with everything you have
strings.拿到U盘，或者让何志强的事曝光: Get the USB drive — or expose what Steven Ho did
strings.挖掘机到了这栋楼的西侧。每一铲下去，三角区都跟着一抖，灰土簌簌地往下落。突然，发: The excavator has reached the west side of the building. Every bite of the bucket makes the triangle shudder and dust sift down. Suddenly the roar of the engine stops. Outside someone is shouting: "Hold it! Everyone hold it! Listen for anyone below!"
strings.挖掘机挪到了北边，可每一铲下去，头顶的楼板还是跟着抖。再这么挖下去，不用等余震，: The excavator has moved round to the north, but every bite of the bucket still makes the slab overhead tremble. If the digging goes on like this, the triangle will come down on its own, aftershock or no.
strings.挖水桶、加固、翻东西时有光，效率高、少受伤；但收不到任何信号: Light for digging out the jug, shoring, searching: faster work and fewer injuries — but no chance of catching a signal
strings.挤压综合征：肢体被压几个小时以后，坏死肌肉释放的钾和肌红蛋白被“关”在受压的部位: Crush syndrome: after a limb has been pinned for a few hours, the potassium and myoglobin released by dying muscle are “locked in” the crushed area. Lift the weight off rashly and they surge into the circulation — the heart may stop on the spot, or hours later. The longer the compression, the greater the danger. Drinking plenty of water beforehand lowers the risk; a tourniquet applied first will usually save the life but not the leg. Professional rescuers put in an IV first, then lift.
strings.挨个看：谁的嘴唇是湿的，谁的衣服上有水渍: Look at each of them: whose lips are wet, whose clothes have a damp patch
strings.掏到一半，上面掉下来一块混凝土，砸在 {actor} 的肩膀上。: Halfway in, a lump of concrete drops from above onto {actor}'s shoulder.
strings.推楼板时被挤伤: Crushed while shoving at the slab
strings.推选一个人钻出去求救: Pick someone to crawl out for help
strings.推选一个人钻进半塌的楼梯间，爬出去找救援队。路上随时可能有落石，也可能根本找不到: Pick one person to crawl into the half-collapsed stairwell and get out to find the rescue teams. Falling debris the whole way — and there may be no way out at all.
strings.摇晃来之前的几秒钟，来福突然跳起来呜呜直叫——好几个人下意识地抱住了头，往柱子边: In the few seconds before the shaking starts, Buddy leaps up whining — several people cover their heads by instinct and shrink back against the column.
strings.摸了半天，只摸到一手灰和碎砖: Groped around for ages and came up with nothing but dust and broken brick
strings.摸黑被碎玻璃割伤: Cut by glass working in the dark
strings.撑开雨伞倒过来接，杯子、文件盒全摆上: Open the umbrella upside down to catch it; set out cups and document boxes
strings.撕一张会议纪要，把她的话一字不落地记下来: Tear off a sheet of the meeting minutes and write down every word
strings.撕下衬衫袖子，蘸点水捂住口鼻: Tear the sleeves off a shirt, wet them, and cover nose and mouth
strings.撬头顶的楼板总归是冒险；可让一个发着烧的孩子一个人待在上面，也是冒险: Prying at the slab overhead is a gamble; but leaving a feverish child alone up there is a gamble too
strings.撬开裂缝，把她接下来: Pry the crack open and get her down
strings.救援现场每隔一阵就会停机静听；那几十秒，才是最要紧的: Rescue sites stop the machines every so often to listen; those few dozen seconds are what matters
strings.救援通道打通了。一个背着药箱的救援医生先爬了进来，看见老刘腿上的楼板，立刻喊：“: The rescue tunnel is through. A rescue doctor with a medical pack crawls in first, sees the slab on Dustin’s legs and shouts at once: “Nobody touch him!” — fluids have to go in first, then the slab lifted with hydraulic jacks: two hours at least. Do the others get out, or stay with him?
strings.救援通道打通了。可从三角区里爬出来的人，出了洞口就各走各的，谁也没有回头看别人一: The rescue tunnel was through. But the people who crawled out of the triangle went their separate ways, and not one looked back. The food eaten in the dark, the person pushed out, the hard words in the dark — all of it stayed in that 1.2-metre gap. Alive: {survivors}. Never came out: {dead}. Later a TV station tried to make a programme about people helping each other under the rubble and rang them one by one. Not one agreed to be interviewed.
strings.救援通道打通了。活着被抬出废墟的人：{survivors}。留在三角区里的：{d: The rescue tunnel was through. Lifted out of the rubble alive: {survivors}. Left in the triangle: {dead}. Many years later the survivors still wake in the night and reach up over their heads — and their hands find a ceiling, not a floor slab.
strings.救援队会先输液再搬: They will put in an IV before they move anyone
strings.救援队员把最后一个人托出洞口的时候，外面的天光刺得所有人睁不开眼。担架、盐水、毯: When the rescuers lifted the last person out of the gap, the daylight outside was blinding. Stretchers, IV lines, blankets, and beyond the cordon a mass of crying faces. {survivors} — not one missing. A doctor said afterwards that what kept you alive was that jug of water, the knocking, and that no one gave up on anyone.
strings.救援队员趴在洞口，一个一个地喊名字。被喊到的人，回头看了一眼，才往上爬。: The rescuers lie at the mouth of the hole and call names, one by one. The ones who are called look back once, then climb.
strings.救援队在锦华大厦的废墟上搜了一遍又一遍，生命探测仪始终没有等到回应。很多天以后，: The rescue teams searched the ruin of Jinhua Tower over and over, and the life-detection gear never got an answer. Many days later the workers clearing the rubble found the triangular gap on the third floor: an empty water jug lying under the conference table, and the column covered in dents knocked into it by a length of steel pipe.
strings.救援队大约在震后 24–48 小时到达这片街区，但周围塌了很多栋楼。每回合被定位: Rescue teams reach the district roughly 24–48 hours after the quake, but many buildings around you have collapsed. Each round, the chance of being located depends on the “distress signal” you have put out: tapping is cheap; shouting is easier to confirm but costs more water; a text message, once it gets through, works best. The signal slowly fades. Once you are located, the rescuers still need a day or two to cut a passage through, and aftershocks and heavy rain make them stop work.
strings.救援队定位到你们以后，从外面往三角区挖的进度。余震和大雨会让他们停工。: Once the rescuers have located you: how far they have dug from outside toward the triangle. Aftershocks and heavy rain make them stop work.
strings.救援队顶楼板用的就是这种木垛；可要拆桌子、码大半天，又累又渴，搬东西时楼板会晃: Rescue teams prop slabs with exactly this kind of crib; but breaking the table and stacking it takes half a day, it is thirsty work, and the slab shifts while you move things
strings.敲了一遍又一遍，墙那边再也没有回音。: Again and again the pipe goes out, and nothing ever comes back.
strings.敲了很久很久，墙那边终于传来两下很轻的敲击。陈阿姨还活着。: For a long, long time nothing; then at last two faint knocks come back. Auntie Chen is alive.
strings.敲击声能顺着钢筋传出去；可挖掘机那么响，开机器的人未必听得见。又累又渴: Knocking travels along the steel; but over that engine the driver may not hear it. Tiring, and thirsty work
strings.文件夹卷成的管子又一次塞进了裂缝。上面先是没有动静，然后传来了咕咚咕咚的吞咽声。: The folder tube goes into the crack again. For a moment there is nothing; then the sound of gulping.
strings.文件柜在楼板底下被压弯以后，最晚哪个回合会折（内部计数）。: The latest round the buckling cabinet can last under the slab (internal counter).
strings.文件柜终于被撬开了。那桶 18.9 升的桶装水完好无损，蓝色的桶身上全是灰。有人: At last the filing cabinet is pried away. The 18.9 L jug is intact, its blue plastic caked in dust. Someone wipes it with a palm and suddenly bursts into tears.
strings.文件柜被压垮，东头的楼板坐了下来: The cabinet folded and the east end of the slab came down
strings.文件柜被压垮，楼板坐了下来: The cabinet folded and the slab came down
strings.新鲜空气会灌进来，粉尘少很多；外面的人也更容易听见: Fresh air will come in and the dust will thin out a lot; and people outside will hear you more easily
strings.新鲜空气能压住粉尘，外面也更容易听见这里；可掏墙会让三角区跟着晃: Fresh air will keep the dust down and people outside will hear this place more easily; but digging will shake the triangle
strings.明天推选人选。爬出去的人要穿过半塌的楼梯间: Choose who goes tomorrow. Whoever crawls out has to get through the half-collapsed stairwell
strings.最后一部开着等信号的手机也没电了，屏幕黑了下去。: The last phone left on for a signal died too, and its screen went black.
strings.最容易被听见，但很耗水和力气: Easiest to hear, but it burns water and strength
strings.最有用的一条短信: The most useful text there is
strings.最符合救援规范，可没人知道救援队什么时候到: Textbook practice — but nobody knows when the rescue team will arrive
strings.最符合救援规范，可老刘得一直被压着，熬到救援队来: Textbook rescue practice — but Dustin stays pinned, and has to last until the rescuers arrive
strings.最符合救援规范，可要被压着熬到救援队来: Textbook rescue practice — but it means staying pinned until they arrive
strings.最虚弱的人先被一点点托了出去。剩下的人在黑暗里数着时间，一个，又一个。: The weakest are lifted out one small movement at a time. The others count the time in the dark. One. And another.
strings.最需要救治的人先走: The ones who need treatment most leave first
strings.有人在黑暗里握住了她的手，握了很久。: Someone in the dark takes her hand, and holds it a long time.
strings.有人把手机举在裂缝口，一遍一遍地按“重新发送”。: Someone holds the phone at the crack and presses Resend, again and again.
strings.有人挨着老陶坐了下来，肩膀碰着肩膀。: Someone sits down beside Tom, shoulder against shoulder.
strings.有人握住了 {actor} 的手：“跟着我，吸——呼——”过了很久，{actor: Someone takes {actor}’s hand: “With me. In — and out —” It is a long time before {actor}’s hand stops shaking.
strings.有人摸黑写下了那几行字，折好，塞进了贴身的口袋。: Someone writes the lines down in the dark, folds the paper and tucks it into an inside pocket.
strings.有人用塑料文件夹把裂缝塞住了。雨声还在头顶响，可身上是干的。: Someone jams plastic folders into the crack. The rain is still loud overhead, but they are dry.
strings.有人看见领头人半夜把水杯递到了何志强手里。: Someone saw the leader hand a cup of water to Steven Ho in the middle of the night.
strings.有他在，大家心里就有底；可吊楼板的时候，下面谁也说不准: With him here everyone feels steadier; but when the slab is lifted, nothing down here is certain
strings.有信号的话，也许能打通；家里人会去找救援队: With signal, it might get through; the family would go to the rescue teams
strings.朵朵不太记得废墟里的事了，只记得黑，记得有人一直跟她说话、陪她数数。她妈妈每年五: Daisy doesn’t remember much about being under the rubble — only the dark, and that someone kept talking to her and counting with her. Every May her mother takes her to sweep Teacher Wu’s grave. Daisy sets a sweet on the headstone and says quietly, “Teacher Wu, you held me so tight that day.”
strings.朵朵是第一个被托出洞口的。几十只手从洞口一直排到警戒线，一个传一个，把那个裹着银: Daisy was the first one lifted out of the gap. Dozens of hands ran from the opening to the cordon, passing that small body wrapped in a silver blanket from one to the next. The next day the photograph was on the front page of a lot of papers. What the picture doesn’t show is the people still under the opening, arms raised, who had not come out themselves. Alive: {survivors}. Did not live to see it: {dead}.
strings.朵朵是第一个被托出洞口的。第二天，一张照片上了很多报纸：一个满脸是灰的救援队员抱: Daisy was the first one lifted out of the gap. The next day a photograph ran in a lot of papers: a rescue worker grey with dust carrying a little girl wrapped in a silver emergency blanket, a bottle of cold Coke clutched in her hand. She went on into second grade. At every school earthquake drill she is the first one under a desk, and then she counts quietly.
strings.朵朵的妈妈后来去过很多次锦华大厦的旧址。新楼打地基的时候，她在围挡外面放了一个粉: Daisy’s mother went back to the site of Jinhua Tower many times. While they were pouring the foundations of the new building she left a little pink schoolbag outside the hoarding, with a bottle of cold Coke in it and a first-grade certificate of merit. That afternoon at three o’clock she stood outside the hoarding for a long time. Three o’clock was when she had promised to come and pick up her daughter.
strings.朵朵被裹在一条银色的保温毯里，被一双双手托着送出了洞口。洞口外面，一个女人的哭声: Daisy, wrapped in a silver emergency blanket, is passed out through the gap on a dozen hands. Outside, a woman’s wail goes up. The rest follow, one after another.
strings.来福先是竖着耳朵听，然后突然冲着裂缝狂叫起来。上面的搜救犬立刻回应，两条狗隔着几: Buddy listens first, ears up, then suddenly barks wildly at the crack. The search dog answers at once, and the two of them go back and forth through metres of rubble, one bark after another.
strings.来福后来被送回了老刘在达州乡下的家。它再也不肯进任何一栋楼，夜里只睡在院坝里，一: Buddy was sent back to Dustin’s home in the Dazhou countryside. He would not go into any building again; at night he slept only in the yard, and at the least sound he would scramble up and stare at the sky, shaking. The villagers said dogs remember earthquakes longer than people do.
strings.来福在西北角刨了大半天。今天，它刨开的那个小洞里透进来一丝风，还有隐隐约约的车声: Buddy has been digging in the northwest corner most of the day. Today a breath of air comes through the little hole he has opened, and, faintly, the sound of traffic. The hole is only as wide as a bowl — too small for a person, just wide enough for a dog to squeeze through.
strings.来福竖着耳朵听了两秒，突然冲着裂缝狂叫起来。: Buddy listens, ears up, for two seconds, then bursts into frantic barking at the crack.
strings.来福被抱了回来，趴回老刘身边，舔了舔他的手。: Buddy is carried back and lies down beside Dustin again, and licks his hand.
strings.来福被推出洞口，又钻回来两次。最后一次，它在洞口站了很久，才转身不见了。: Buddy is pushed out through the hole and squeezes back in twice. The last time, he stands at the opening for a long while before turning and disappearing.
strings.林小雨低着头说了声“谢谢”，声音小得几乎听不见。: Lily Lin says “thank you” without lifting her head, in a voice barely there.
strings.林小雨在流血。她自己说，最要紧的是平躺、别再脱水——可水就这么多，所有人的嘴唇都: Lily Lin is bleeding. She says it herself: what matters most is lying flat and not getting any more dehydrated. But there is only so much water, and everyone's lips are cracked.
strings.林小雨怀孕的事，大家都知道了。有人小声提议：从今天起，水给她多分一份。: Everyone knows now that Lily Lin is pregnant. Someone suggests, quietly, that from today she gets a bigger share of the water.
strings.林小雨想说什么，没说出来，只是一直点头。: Lily Lin tries to say something, cannot, and only keeps nodding.
strings.林小雨自己找准了血管，冯建军只帮她按住了胶布。: Lily Lin finds the vein herself; all Jim Feng does is hold the tape for her.
strings.某市城南·锦华大厦 3 楼东侧会议室: South side of the city · Jinhua Tower, 3rd floor, east conference room
strings.柜子真塌了也砸不着人；可西头更矮更挤，被压着、走不动的人挪不过去: If the cabinet goes, it will not land on anyone; but the west end is lower and more cramped, and anyone pinned or unable to walk stays where they are
strings.柜子里的另一个小急救包: Another small first-aid pouch from a cabinet
strings.柜子顶上去的那一刻，又一块碎板滑了下来，压在 {target} 的胳膊上。: The moment the cabinet was up, another broken slab slid down and landed on {target}’s arm.
strings.桌腿“咔”地一声弯了，楼板滑回去，重重地压回老刘腿上。{actor} 的手被夹在: The table leg bends with a crack, the slab slides back and slams down on Dustin’s legs again. {actor}’s hand is caught underneath.
strings.桌面拆成了一条一条的木板，两根一层，横竖交错，一层一层码到了楼板底下。秦朗用最后: The tabletop is broken into planks, laid two to a layer, crosswise and lengthwise, layer on layer up to the slab. Leonard Qin taps the last wedge home and lets out a long breath. "Now it's not taking the weight on its own."
strings.桶是挖出来了，可桶底被柜角砸出一道裂缝，地毯湿了一大片。剩下的水大概只有十来升。: The jug is out, but the corner of the cabinet has split its base and the carpet is soaked. Maybe ten litres or so are left.
strings.椅子、公文包、成摞的文件，一样一样塞进楼板底下。: Chairs, briefcases, stacks of files go in under the slab one after another.
strings.楼板一抬，头顶落下一片碎块，砸在 {actor} 身上。: As the slab lifts, a shower of debris comes down from overhead onto {actor}.
strings.楼板一松，头顶塌下来一片碎块，砸在 {actor} 身上。: The moment the slab shifts, a shower of debris comes down from overhead and lands on {actor}.
strings.楼板刚被撬开，{actor} 的脸一下子白了，抓着旁边人的手说了句“心口……”，: The moment the slab comes up, {actor} goes white, grips the nearest hand, says, “My chest…” — and does not let go again.
strings.楼板刚被撬开，老刘“啊”了一声，身子一挺，就再也没有动静了。有人扑上去按他的胸口: The moment the slab comes up, Dustin says “ah —”, his body arches, and then he is still. Someone throws herself onto his chest and presses, for a long, long time.
strings.楼板吊开，通道能快一大截；他走了，下面就只剩你们自己: With the slab lifted the tunnel goes far faster; and once he’s gone, you are on your own down here
strings.楼板坐下来的那一下，{actor} 正缩在柜子边上。: When the slab came down, {actor} was curled up right beside the cabinet.
strings.楼板缝里漏进来一丝天光。白天闷热，夜里凉下来。: A thread of daylight leaks in through the cracks in the slab. Stifling by day, cooler at night.
strings.楼梯间落石砸伤: Struck by falling debris in the stairwell
strings.楼里的人……都跑出去了没得？: The people in the building… did they all get out?
strings.每一铲落下来，所有人都跟着抖一下。: Every time the bucket comes down, they all flinch with it.
strings.每个人从自己那份里匀一口给她: Everyone gives her one mouthful from their own share
strings.每个人脸上都捂了一块湿布，呼吸声闷闷的，可咳嗽少了。: Everyone has a wet cloth over their face; their breathing sounds muffled, but the coughing drops off.
strings.每个人都对着屏幕打了很久的字，又删掉，又重打。: Everyone types at their screen for a long time, deletes it, types it again.
strings.每个人都能润一润嗓子；可谁也解决不了根本: Everyone gets their throat wet; but it fixes nothing
strings.每人先给家里发一条短信报平安: Everyone sends one text home to say they are alive
strings.每人立刻喝下约 0.8 升；桶里剩下的少了，可喝进肚子里的不会漏: Everyone drinks about 0.8 L at once; there is less left in the jug, but what is in your stomach can’t leak out
strings.每人能喝上几口，但渗过废墟的水很脏: A few mouthfuls each — but water that has filtered through rubble is filthy
strings.每回合从公共的水里多给她一点；别人就少一点: A little more from the shared water every shift; a little less for everyone else
strings.每回合从公共的水里多给她约 0.15 升: About 0.15 L a round out of the common supply
strings.每回合耗电约 5%；信号一恢复，求救短信就可能自己发出去。干活只能摸黑: Drains about 5% a round; the text may go out by itself the moment the network comes back. All work is done in the dark.
strings.每年清明，他都要回一趟达州，在老刘的坟前点三根烟，自己抽一根，给老刘留两根。他后: Every Qingming he goes back to Dazhou, lights three cigarettes at Dustin’s grave, smokes one himself and leaves two for Dustin. He doesn’t deliver any more. He runs a little restaurant in his home town, and the signature dish is twice-cooked pork over rice.
strings.水 +4 升，再加一些能直接喝的葡萄糖液: Water +4 L, plus some glucose drink you can take straight
strings.水喂进去了一大半。半夜，老刘的呼吸忽然停了。: Most of the water goes in. In the middle of the night, Dustin stops breathing.
strings.水喂进去了大半。天快亮的时候，{actor} 的呼吸停了。: Most of the water goes in. Towards dawn, {actor} stops breathing.
strings.水已经喝光了。黑暗里有人哑着嗓子说：“听说当年汶川，有人就是靠喝自己的尿撑下来的: The water is gone. Out of the dark someone says, hoarse, “I heard that in Wenchuan, people survived on their own urine.” Nobody answers. Everybody is thinking about it.
strings.水桶被挪到了领头人身边。从那以后，每一口水都要当着所有人的面倒。: The jug is moved next to the leader. From then on, every mouthful is poured in front of everyone.
strings.求他出去以后马上告诉救援队：三楼东侧有活人: Beg him to tell the rescue teams the moment he gets out: there are living people on the east side of the third floor
strings.求他带一个人从管道井爬出去报信: Ask him to take one person out through the pipe shaft to raise the alarm
strings.求大家：现在就把板子撬开: Beg them: pry the slab off now
strings.汪！汪汪！（它冲着外面叫了几声，又停下来，歪着头听。）: Woof! Woof woof! (He barks a few times at the outside, stops, and cocks his head to listen.)
strings.没事儿，有我呢。咱慢慢来。: It’s all right. I’m here. We’ll take it slow.
strings.没人会知道；可搬东西、挖碎砖，都是往下用力: No one will know; but lifting and digging both mean bearing down
strings.没有人再去敲那面墙，可每个人都在听。: Nobody knocks on that wall again, but everyone is listening.
strings.没有人再回答上面的声音。哭声持续了很久，越来越弱，后来就没有了。: Nobody answers the voice above any more. The crying goes on for a long time, weaker and weaker, and then stops.
strings.没有人再把水递给老刘。他闭着眼睛，像是睡着了。: Nobody offers Dustin water again. He closes his eyes, as if asleep.
strings.没有人再提这件事，可那天以后，大家睡觉时都朝着水桶。: No one brings it up again, but from that day on they all sleep facing the jug.
strings.没有人去动那块楼板。{protagonist} 盯着头顶，过了很久才说：“好，我: Nobody touches the slab. {protagonist} stares up at the ceiling, and after a long time says, “All right. I’ll wait.”
strings.没有人去动那块楼板。老刘把脸转向墙，过了很久，小声说了句：“晓得了，莫怪你们。”: Nobody touches the slab. Dustin turns his face to the wall, and after a long time says quietly, “I hear you. Don’t blame yourselves.”
strings.没有人说话。黑暗里，只听得见水桶里的水轻轻晃荡的声音。: Nobody speaks. In the dark, all they can hear is the water sloshing gently in the jug.
strings.没有任何预兆，三角区松动的那一角自己塌了。{actor} 没来得及躲开。: Without warning, the loose corner of the triangle came down on its own. {actor} didn’t get clear in time.
strings.河北唐山人，开了半辈子农机修理铺。1976 年唐山大地震那年他九岁，在自家塌下来: Born in Tangshan, Hebei; he ran an agricultural machinery repair shop for half his life. He was nine in 1976, the year of the Tangshan earthquake, and lay buried for three days under his own family’s house until a young PLA soldier dug him out with his bare hands.
