When he heard about the quake here he drove through the night with a dozen men from his village in two pickup trucks and joined a civilian rescue team. Tall and lean, in a yellow hard hat with the paint flaking off.
strings.活着出去，并且保住包里的U盘: Get out alive, and keep the USB drive in your bag
strings.活着被抬出废墟的人：{survivors}。没能出来的：{dead}。三个月后，: Lifted out of the rubble alive: {survivors}. Never came out: {dead}. Three months later the findings on the illegal floors and the forged acceptance certificates made the news. Among the names signed on those certificates was one you all knew well.
strings.清早一清点，水桶里的水比昨晚少了一截。有人半夜偷喝了。: The morning count shows the water in the jug has dropped since the night before. Someone drank in the dark.
strings.清理废墟的工人在三角区里找到了来福，它的头还朝着那道裂缝。工人们把它埋在了大厦后: The workers clearing the rubble found Buddy inside the triangle, his head still turned toward that crack. They buried him in the planting strip behind the tower, and stuck a length of rebar in the ground to mark the spot.
strings.灰还没落定。手机电筒的光里，保安老刘的两条小腿被一块斜塌下来的楼板死死压着，他咬: The dust has not settled yet. In the light of a phone torch, the guard Dustin’s shins are pinned fast under a slab that came down at an angle. He says through his teeth, “It’s nothing. Doesn’t hurt.” Leonard Qin crawls over and takes a look: “If we’re going to pry it, it has to be now. Leave it a few hours and when we lift it the man could just drop dead. But this slab might also be what’s holding the ceiling up over us.”
strings.灰还没落定，秦朗就开了口，声音不大，每个字都很硬：“从现在起，这个夹缝里哪块板子: Before the dust has settled Leonard Qin speaks, not loudly, every word hard. "From now on, which slab can be touched, where we dig, who sleeps where: you listen to me. Eight years as a combat engineer. I've taken down more condemned buildings than you've ever seen." He looks at Steven Ho. "As for how many floors this building was meant to have, we can settle that once we're out."
strings.爪子刨土的声音渐渐远了。: The sound of claws on rubble slowly moves away.
strings.爬到一半，头顶的楼梯板塌下来一截。{actor} 没能爬出来。: Halfway up, a section of stair slab comes down overhead. {actor} never gets out.
strings.爱面子、习惯发号施令，嘴上总说“大家放心”，心里最怕的是出去以后要担责任。危急时: Proud and used to giving orders. He keeps saying “don’t worry, everyone”, but what he fears most is being held responsible once they get out. In a crisis he shifts the blame first, yet he is not without guilt: when no one is looking, he stares blankly at the crack overhead.
strings.狗叫声在人耳朵里格外扎: A dog's bark cuts through to human ears
strings.狗听得懂狗；来福一叫，上面的搜救犬就有了方向: A dog understands a dog; once Buddy barks, the search dog above has a direction
strings.狗在头顶停住了，冲着裂缝叫个不停。: The dog stops directly overhead and barks and barks at the crack.
strings.狗认路，也许能把人引过来；也许它跑了就不回来——它是老刘的伴: A dog knows the way; he might bring people back — or he might run and never return. He is Dustin’s companion.
strings.玩家被压的时间: Hours a player has been pinned
strings.现在就撬开，趁压得还不久: Pry it open now, while it hasn’t been long
strings.用一截钢管有节奏地敲柱子和水管：三下一停。敲击声能顺着钢筋混凝土传得很远，比喊叫: Tap a length of steel pipe against the column and the water pipes in a rhythm: three knocks, then a pause. Sound travels a long way through reinforced concrete, and tapping costs far less strength than shouting. Until the rescuers are close, few people will hear it.
strings.用剩下的电发短信: Use the remaining charge to send a text
strings.用卷起来的文件夹当管子，水和饼干都递得上去——她也就成了一张要分水的嘴；裂缝不动: Rolled-up folders work as a tube; water and biscuits can go up — and she becomes one more mouth to share water with; the crack stays as it is, but she is alone up there, next to Teacher Wu
strings.用掉 1.5 升公共的水，能降低风险: Uses 1.5 L of the shared water; lowers the risk
strings.用掉 1.5 升水，提前补水能降低风险: Uses 1.5 L of water; fluids beforehand lower the risk
strings.用掉 2 升水。冲淡血里的钾，也许能救他一命: Uses 2 L of water. Diluting the potassium in his blood might save his life
strings.用掉 2 升水。提前补水能冲淡血里的钾，降低风险: Uses 2 L of water. Fluids beforehand dilute the potassium in the blood and lower the risk
strings.用掉 2 升水，冲淡血里的钾: Uses 2 L of water; dilutes the potassium in the blood
strings.用掉约 0.6 升水；以后粉尘的伤害会小很多: Uses about 0.6 L of water; the dust will do much less harm after this
strings.用胶带和塑料袋把口子缠上: Tape up the hole with plastic bags
strings.用钢管敲柱子：三下，停，再三下: Knock the pipe against the column: three, pause, three.
strings.用领带、丝巾干捂着: Cover up dry with ties and scarves
strings.电是命；他不会拦你: Charge is life; he will not stop you
strings.电话居然通了。{actor} 对着手机说了一句“幺儿，爸爸没得事”，后面的话就说: The call actually goes through. {actor} says into the phone, “Little one, Papa’s all right,” and then can’t say anything else. On the other end his wife, crying, writes down the name of the tower and the floor.
strings.电话居然通了。老陶对着话筒“嫂子……”了一声，就再也说不下去。过了很久，他才哑着: The call actually connects. Tom gets as far as "Sister-in-law..." and can go no further. A long time later, his voice gone to gravel, he gives the building's name: Jinhua Tower, third floor, east side, people still alive.
strings.电话没有打通。{actor} 盯着屏幕上女儿的照片，看了很久。: The call doesn’t go through. {actor} stares at the photo of his daughter on the screen for a long time.
strings.电话那头的人哭得说不出话。{actor} 一遍一遍地说：“我没事，我没事。”: The person on the other end is crying too hard to speak. {actor} says it over and over: “I’m fine. I’m fine.”
strings.电量 +80；能把楼板的走向说给救援队听，通道会挖得快一些: Charge +80; you can talk the rescuers through the lie of the slabs, and they will cut the tunnel faster
strings.电锤凿到第四个钟头，头顶一块松掉的预制板突然滑了下来。冯建军把离他最近的人往柱子: In the fourth hour of hammering, a loosened precast panel slides down overhead. Jim Feng shoves the nearest person toward the column. He doesn’t get clear himself.
strings.电锤震下来一块碎板，砸在冯建军的肩膀上。他咬着牙说：“没事儿，蹭了一下。”: The hammer shakes a broken slab loose; it lands on Jim Feng’s shoulder. He says through his teeth, “It’s nothing. Just grazed me.”
strings.留着它：余震前它总是第一个发抖: Keep him: he always trembles first before an aftershock
strings.白光在裂缝口一下一下地闪：三短，三长，三短。: White light blinks at the mouth of the crack: three short, three long, three short.
strings.白天未必看得见；还要费电: It may not show in daylight; and it costs battery
strings.皮带勒上了，楼板撬开了，可老刘还是没能挺过去。: The belts went on and the slab came up, and Dustin still didn’t make it.
strings.直接仰着头接着喝: Tip your head back and drink it straight
strings.省下力气和口水，可心里那道坎过不去: Saves strength and spit, but it is a thing you can’t get past in yourself
strings.省下水，省下力气；这件事会跟着每个人一辈子: Saves water and strength; and this is a thing that will follow every one of them for life
strings.省下的是自己的命；可这句话说出口，就收不回来: What you save is your own life; but once said, it cannot be taken back
strings.省力气，就看狗的本事了: Saves strength; it comes down to the dog’s nose
strings.省力气；能不能被发现，就看他们下一次停机: It saves strength; whether you are found depends on the next time they stop
strings.省力，敲击声能顺着钢筋传出去: Cheap in strength, and the knocking carries out along the rebar
strings.省力，最适合静默搜听: Cheap in strength — the best answer to a silence-and-listen
strings.省着力气，他们会回来的: Save your strength. They’ll come back.
strings.省着力气：等机器一停，再一起敲、一起喊: Save your strength: when the machines stop, everyone knocks and shouts together
strings.看手巧不巧：缠住了只漏一点，缠不住会漏掉一大半: Depends on steady hands: patched, it only drips; botched, half of it runs away
strings.看谁能说动他: See who can get through to him
strings.短信发出去了！过了半个小时，回过来一条：“收到。救援队马上回来。”: The text went out! Half an hour later a reply came back: “Received. Rescue team coming back.”
strings.碎块砸下来的时候，冯建军弓着背挡在了最前面。: When the debris came down, Jim Feng hunched over and put his back in the way.
strings.离外面的人近一点，也离塌近一点: Closer to the people outside, and closer to a collapse
strings.私下找他要一口: Ask him for a mouthful, privately
strings.私下提醒她：命比包要紧: Warn her privately: your life matters more than the bag
strings.秦朗举着手机电筒，照着那个顶住楼板的铁皮文件柜看了很久，脸色越来越难看：“侧板鼓: Leonard Qin holds up his phone torch and studies the steel filing cabinet propping up the slab for a long time, his face growing darker. "The side panels are bulging. One-millimetre sheet steel, holding several tonnes of slab for all these hours, and it is buckling outwards, bit by bit. One more strong aftershock and it folds like a drinks can."
strings.秦朗只说了一句：“原图纸是十层。”所有人都转过头去看何志强。何志强张了张嘴，什么: Leonard Qin says just one thing: "The original drawings were for ten floors." Every head turns to Steven Ho. Steven Ho opens his mouth, and nothing comes out.
strings.秦朗把那几根还立着的桌腿一根根敲了一遍，在每一根上用口红画了一道杠：“谁要挪这些: Leonard Qin taps each of the table legs still standing, and marks every one with a stripe of lipstick. "Anyone wants to move these, ask me first."
strings.秦朗敲了敲头顶的楼板，冷冷地说：“这楼原图纸是十层，现在是十二层。何总，加盖那两: Leonard Qin raps the slab overhead and says coldly: “The original drawings for this building show ten floors. There are twelve now. Mr Ho, your company did the fit-out on those added floors, didn’t it? And you didn’t know the building couldn’t carry them?” Every head turns to Steven Ho.
strings.秦朗没再说话，只是把电筒关了，侧着耳朵听那个柜子。夜里，它又“咯”地响了一声。: Leonard Qin says nothing more. He switches off the torch and listens to the cabinet. In the night it creaks again.
strings.秦朗点点头，什么也没说，转身去看那个木垛了。: Leonard Qin nods, says nothing, and turns back to the props.
strings.稳妥，但手忙脚乱会洒掉不少: Safe enough — but in the scramble a fair amount will spill
strings.空矿泉水瓶、保温杯、笔筒、文件盒……能装水的东西全都摆满了。: Empty mineral-water bottles, thermoses, pen cups, document boxes… everything that could hold water is filled and standing in a row.
strings.第一个夜里，几部手机的屏幕轮流亮着。加起来的电量不到两部满电，信号格一直是空的。: The first night. Phone screens light up in turn. Between them there is less than two full charges, and the signal bar stays empty. They need a rule: how is the power to be used?
strings.第二天，{actor} 和黄勇谁也没提昨晚的事。: The next day, neither {actor} nor Ken Huang mentions the night before.
strings.第二天，{actor} 开始上吐下泻。: The next day, {actor} starts vomiting and can’t stop.
strings.第二年春节，他和老刘在达州老家喝了一顿酒。老刘喝多了，非要给他磕头，被他一把拽住: The next Spring Festival the two of them drank together back in Dazhou. Dustin got drunk and tried to kowtow to him; Ken Huang hauled him upright. On his daughter’s seventh birthday he finally got a video call through to her. On the screen the little girl asked, “Dad, how come you’ve got so many scars on your face?”
strings.等出去了，我请你们吃唐山的蜂蜜麻糖。: When we’re out of here, I’m treating you all to Tangshan honey pastry.
strings.等出去了，我请你们吃达州的灯影牛肉。: When we get out of here, I’m treating you all to Dazhou beef jerky.
strings.等大家清点完东西，周敏才发现：她一直抱在怀里的黑色公文包，不见了。: By the time they have finished checking their things, Michelle Zhou discovers that the black briefcase she has been holding all along is gone.
strings.等待时被落石砸伤: Struck by falling debris while waiting
strings.等待的时候又来了一次余震，一块碎石砸在 {actor} 背上。: While they wait there is another aftershock, and a lump of broken concrete hits {actor} in the back.
strings.等摇晃停下来，大家才听见 {actor} 在喊——一块落下来的楼板，正好压在了: When the shaking stops, everyone hears {actor} shouting — a slab has come down across {actor.his} shin.
strings.等灰落下来，老刘那边已经没有声音了。: When the dust settles, there is no sound from Old Liu's side any more.
strings.算了，先活着出去再说: Forget it. Get out alive first.
strings.管子塞过去以后，墙那边先是没有动静，接着传来一阵呛咳，然后是一声很轻的：“……谢: After the tube goes through there is silence on the other side, then a fit of coughing, then, very quietly: "...Thank you."
strings.管子里流出来的水带着一股塑料味，可那是大家这辈子喝过最甜的水。: The water from the tube tasted of plastic, but it was the sweetest water any of them had ever drunk.
strings.箱子里的东西会被充公，黄勇会恨你: The contents will be confiscated, and Ken Huang will hate you
strings.粉尘呛得人一直咳，嗓子像被砂纸磨过，吐出来的唾沫都是灰的。: The dust keeps everyone coughing; throats feel scoured with sandpaper and even spit comes out grey.
strings.精明、多疑、嘴硬；见了穿西装的就矮半截，心里又看不起他们。不是坏到骨子里的人，可: Shrewd, suspicious, stubborn. He shrinks in front of men in suits, and despises them all the same. He isn’t rotten to the core; but for days now he has had room for exactly one thought — to make a quick haul out of the chaos and pay off his debts back home. When someone is genuinely kind to him, he doesn’t know what to do with his hands.
strings.结算用的临时计数。: A temporary count used at the end of the round.
strings.给她一个盼头；可她要的不是这个: It gives her something to hope for; it is not what she asked for
strings.缝只撬开了一点点，一块碎板就滑了下来，夹住了 {actor} 的手。上面的哭声一: The crack only opens a little before a broken slab slides down and catches {actor}’s hand. Above, the crying stops dead, and it is a long time before it starts again, quietly.
strings.缝里透进来的光灰蒙蒙的，空气又闷又潮。: The light through the cracks is grey and dim; the air is close and damp.
strings.缝隙外面传来急促的喘气声，还有爪子刨碎石的声音——是搜救犬！它在上面转来转去，好: From outside the gap comes fast, heavy breathing and the sound of claws scrabbling at broken stone — a search-and-rescue dog! It circles up there, as if it has caught a scent.
strings.老刘一口一口地喝，喝到后来直摆手。天快亮的时候，他的心跳慢慢平稳了下来。: Dustin drinks mouthful by mouthful, then waves it away. Towards dawn, his heartbeat steadies.
strings.老刘出院以后，再也没提过那天夜里大家挪到西头去的事。只是每次有人问起，他总要先停: After he left hospital Old Liu never once mentioned the night everyone moved to the west end. Only, whenever anyone asked, he would pause first, and then laugh. "That cabinet and me, we sat it out together, just the two of us."
strings.老刘出院以后，拄着双拐去了黄勇家，把一个摔变了形的外卖保温箱交给了他女儿。小姑娘: After Dustin got out of hospital he went to Ken Huang’s home on two crutches and gave the battered delivery cooler box to his daughter. The little girl asked what it was. Dustin crouched down and said, “It was your dad’s. He stayed down there talking to me for days. Wouldn’t let me sleep.”
strings.老刘在医院做了一个多月的透析，肾慢慢缓了过来，两条腿也保住了，只是走路一瘸一拐。: Dustin spent more than a month on dialysis, and his kidneys slowly came back; both legs were saved, though he walks with a limp now. When the new tower went up on the Jinhua site, the property managers asked him to come back and watch the gate. On his rounds he stops at the east side of the third floor and knocks three times on the wall.
strings.老刘已经被压了 {var.pinned_h}。他的脚早就没了知觉，嘴唇干得裂开了: Dustin has been pinned for {var.pinned_h} now. His feet went numb long ago, his lips are split and dry, and he keeps begging, quietly: “Just pry the slab off… please… I can’t take it any more…”
strings.老刘把递到嘴边的水推开了：“莫给我了，留给年轻人。我这两条腿……出去也是个废人。: Dustin pushes the water away from his lips: “Don’t give it to me. Leave it for the young ones. These legs of mine… I’d be no use to anyone out there.”
strings.老刘熬过了那一夜。他的尿是酱油色的——懂行的人说，那是肾在受苦。: Dustin lives through the night. His urine is the colour of soy sauce — those who know say it is his kidneys suffering.
strings.老刘疼得昏了过去。两条皮带死死勒在他的大腿上——没有人敢去想，那两条腿还保不保得: Dustin passed out from the pain. The two belts stay cinched tight around his thighs — and nobody dares think about whether the legs can still be saved.
strings.老刘的腿被楼板压住的小时数。: How many hours Dustin’s legs have been pinned under the slab.
strings.老刘的骨灰被送回了达州乡下。下葬那天，坟头上放着一包他最爱抽的“娇子”和一顶保安: Dustin’s ashes went back to the countryside in Dazhou. At the burial they put a pack of his favourite Jiaozai cigarettes and a guard’s cap on the grave. In the Jinhua Tower owners’ chat group someone wrote: “That day it was Master Liu who came up to tell us to move the cars. That’s the only reason I ran.” A long row of candles followed.
strings.老刘被拖出来以后，脸色反倒好看了些，还跟大家开了句玩笑。可没过几个小时，他突然说: After Dustin is dragged clear his colour actually looks better, and he jokes with them. But a few hours later he suddenly says his chest feels tight, his hands and feet are numb, and his pulse races and slows by turns… Someone goes white: “Crush syndrome.”
strings.老刘说着说着，声音越来越小。他最后说的是：“楼里的人……都跑出去了没得……”: Dustin’s voice gets smaller as he talks. The last thing he says is: “The people in the building… did they all get out…”
strings.老师说地震的时候要躲到桌子底下。我们躲对了没有？: Teacher said when there’s an earthquake you hide under a desk. Did we hide in the right place?
strings.老板腔，爱说“听我的”“我来安排”“大家放心”，一紧张说话就结巴。: Talks like a boss — “listen to me”, “I’ll handle it”, “don’t worry, everyone” — and stammers when he’s nervous.
strings.老陶上下打量了大家一圈：“胖的莫想，过不去。瘦的、胆子大的，我带一个。先让我歇口: Tom looks them over: “No fat ones. You won’t fit. One thin one, with nerve. I’ll take one. Let me catch my breath first — half the night in that shaft, my legs are water.”
strings.老陶冲着黑暗点了点头，像是在说谢谢，然后消失在检修口里。: Tom nods at the dark, as if to say thank you, and vanishes into the hatch.
strings.老陶叹了口气：“我就说嘛。”他一个人钻回了管道井。: Tom sighs: “Told you.” He crawls back into the shaft alone.
strings.老陶在蛇皮袋里翻充电线，翻出一部屏幕裂了的手机，顺手按亮——然后整个人僵住了。锁: Tom is rummaging in his sack for a charging cable when he pulls out a phone with a cracked screen and thumbs it on. Then he goes rigid. The lock-screen photo is of himself, and a young man in a graduation cap: his nephew, the day he graduated. He picked this phone up from under a crushed desk on the ninth floor.
strings.老陶想了想，把撬棍靠在墙上，一屁股坐了下来：“要得嘛，反正外头也乱。”他从袋子里: Tom thinks about it, leans the crowbar against the wall and sits down with a thump: “All right then. It’s a mess out there anyway.” He digs a sausage out of his sack, breaks it into pieces and hands them round.
strings.老陶愣了一下，“嘿嘿”笑了一声：“要得。”然后钻进了检修口。: Tom pauses, gives a little “heh heh”: “All right.” Then he is into the hatch.
strings.老陶把人送到车库口，没等救援队员过来，就背着蛇皮袋钻进了人群。: Tom delivers them to the garage mouth and, before the rescuers can reach him, shoulders his sack and melts into the crowd.
strings.老陶抱着那部手机，很久没有出声。后来他把蛇皮袋拖过来，把里面的手机、电脑、钱包一: Tom holds the phone for a long time without a sound. Then he drags the sack over and lays out the phones, laptops and wallets on the floor one by one. "All someone else's... all of it belongs to someone." He pushes every power bank across to them.
strings.老陶是最后一个从洞口爬出来的。他把蛇皮袋放在警戒线边上，对着民警伸出了两只手腕。: Tom was the last one out of the gap. He set the woven sack down by the cordon tape and held out both wrists to the police. Every item in it was eventually returned to its owner. The day the company on the ninth floor held its memorial, someone saw him standing in the back row, for a long time.
strings.老陶歇够了，把头灯拧亮：“管道井窄得很，有的地方要侧着身子、憋着气才挤得过去。肩: When Tom has rested enough he turns up his headlamp: “That shaft is narrow. In places you go sideways and hold your breath to get through. Broad shoulders, injured — don’t try. I take one. One.” Pick who crawls out with him to raise the alarm.
strings.老陶比看上去有劲得多。撬棍一抡，{actor} 的小臂上豁开一道口子。等大家回过: Tom is far stronger than he looks. One swing of the crowbar opens {actor}’s forearm. By the time the others gather their wits he has dragged the sack back into the shaft — and taken half a bottle of water off the table with him.
strings.老陶犹豫了一下，点了点头：“要得，我出去就喊人。”他把蛇皮袋往背上一甩，又钻回了: Tom hesitates, then nods: “All right. I’ll shout for help the moment I’m out.” He swings the sack onto his back and crawls back into the shaft.
strings.老陶甩开拽着袋子的那只手，一头钻进了管道井。: Tom wrenches the sack free of the hand holding it and dives into the shaft.
strings.老陶的头灯在管道井里晃了几下，就看不见了。: Tom’s headlamp wavers a few times in the shaft, and is gone.
strings.老陶的蛇皮袋后来交到了派出所。里面的手机、电脑、钱包一件件找到了失主。袋子最底下: Tom’s sack was handed in at the police station. The phones, laptops and wallets inside were returned to their owners one by one. At the very bottom was a crumpled IOU and a photograph of a woman holding a child. Nobody ever came to claim them.
strings.老陶看了看大家，什么也没说，一个人钻回了管道井。: Tom looks at them all, says nothing, and crawls back into the shaft alone.
strings.老陶看着那部手机，嘴唇哆嗦了半天。: Tom stares at the phone, his lips trembling.
strings.胆小、怕添麻烦，什么都憋在心里；可一碰到伤员就会变得冷静、专业。被逼到绝境时会突: Timid, afraid of being a nuisance, keeping everything bottled up — but put her in front of a casualty and she turns calm and professional. Pushed to the limit, she can suddenly explode.
strings.胶带一沾水就滑开了。等大家手忙脚乱地把桶扶正，地毯已经吸饱了水。: The tape slid off the moment it got wet. By the time they had the jug upright again, the carpet had soaked up its fill.
strings.能动的人一个一个蹭到了西头。东头只剩下挪不动的人，和那个一点一点往外鼓的柜子。: Everyone who can move edges along to the west end. Left in the east are those who cannot move, and the cabinet, bulging a little further.
strings.能动的人一个接一个钻进了楼梯间。留下的人握了握他们的手，说：“出去了，记得叫人来: One by one those who can move crawl into the stairwell. Those staying behind shake their hands and say, “When you’re out, make sure they come.”
strings.能听见声音，比纸上的字多；要费不少电: They can hear your voice, and there is more than paper can hold; it costs a lot of charge
strings.能快一点，可最弱的人要在里面等到最后: Quicker — but the weakest wait until the very end
strings.能把楼板再顶住一点；可下沉还没停，伸手进去的人可能被夹住: It may hold the slab a little; but it is still settling, and hands that go in may be caught
strings.能接到一两升水，可接水的地方都湿透了，夜里会冷: Catches a litre or two — but the catching place ends up soaked through, and the night will be cold
strings.能用的东西不多：几个人抽屉里的零食、一个办公室急救箱、一把长柄雨伞、几部电量不多: There is little to work with: snacks from a few desk drawers, an office first-aid kit, a long-handled umbrella, a few phones low on charge — no bars. In the corner, an 18.9 L water-cooler jug is pinned under the toppled filing cabinet. It will have to be dug out.
strings.能走的人先出去，老刘交给医生: Everyone who can walk goes out; the doctor stays with Dustin
strings.腿？早就没得感觉了。没得感觉好，没得感觉就不疼。: Legs? Can’t feel them any more. That’s good. Can’t feel them, can’t hurt.
strings.自己留着，谁也别想动: Keep it for yourself; nobody touches it
strings.莫得事，不疼。真的不疼。: It’s nothing. Doesn’t hurt. Really, it doesn’t hurt.
strings.蛇皮袋被拖了过去。老陶看着那些手机一部一部被拿走，一动没动，手里只攥着那一部。: The sack is dragged away. Tom watches the phones taken one by one without moving, clutching just the one.
strings.袋子里装的可能是大家的水和手机；他手边还有撬棍: The sack may hold everyone’s water and phones; and he still has the crowbar within reach
strings.被推出洞口以后，来福再也没有回来。后来有个救援队员说，那几天总有一条脖子上缠着胶: After he was pushed out through the gap, Buddy never came back. Later a rescuer said that for days there had been a yellow dog with tape round its neck barking at Jinhua Tower from outside the cordon; it wouldn’t be driven off, and wouldn’t eat anything they offered it.
strings.装睡，让他走: Pretend to be asleep and let him go
strings.西墙根的检修口里传来铁器刮擦的声音。一道头灯的光晃了进来——一个黑瘦的男人从管道: From the inspection hatch at the foot of the west wall comes the scrape of iron. A headlamp beam wavers in — a wiry, dark man climbs out of the pipe shaft, a bulging woven sack on his back and a crowbar in his hand. He stares at you for several seconds before giving a little “heh heh”: “No need to get nervous, everyone. I… I came to find my nephew. He works in this building.” The neck of the sack shows half a laptop.
strings.西边传来一种新的声音：不是电锤，也不是喊话，是挖掘机的履带碾过碎砖的“咔啦”声，: A new sound from the west: not a breaker, not a loudhailer, but excavator tracks grinding over broken brick, and a bucket lifting a whole slab and dropping it, booming, into a lorry. Someone says hoarsely: "Seventy-two hours are up... do they think there's nobody alive round here any more?"
strings.要说的话，出去以后当面说: Whatever you have to say, say it face to face when we’re out
strings.要费掉一大截电，看信号: It burns a lot of charge, and depends on the signal
strings.认人、护主，除了老刘谁的话都不太听；见了黄勇摇尾巴，见了穿西装的就龇牙。余震来之: He knows people, and he guards his own. He barely takes orders from anyone but Dustin. He wags his tail at Ken Huang, and bares his teeth at anyone in a suit. In the few seconds before an aftershock he is always the first to stand, trembling all over.
strings.让 {protagonist} 平躺、保暖，别再挪动: Lay {protagonist} flat, keep {protagonist.him} warm, don’t move {protagonist.him} again
strings.让他出去：他也有家，外面还有别的楼等着他: Tell him to go: he has a family, and other buildings waiting
strings.让他平躺、保暖，别再挪动他: Lay him flat, keep him warm, don’t move him again
strings.让他留下：外面余震不断，管道井随时会塌，一起等救援: Ask him to stay: aftershocks keep coming, the shaft could collapse at any moment, wait for rescue together
strings.让别人撑得住，自己会累一点: It holds the others up; it costs you
strings.让大家看清他是什么人: Let them all see what he is
strings.让大家轮流劝他: Have everyone take turns persuading him
strings.让她一个人待一会儿: Leave her alone for a while
strings.让她别哭、别动，省着力气等救援队: Tell her to stop crying and keep still, and save her strength for the rescuers
strings.让她喊，喊得越响越好: Let her shout, as loud as she can
strings.让她在上面再坚持一下：上面那块地方也许比下面结实: Tell her to hold on up there; the space above may be stronger than down here
strings.让她摸摸吴老师身上有没有包，把吃的喝的递下来: Have her feel whether Teacher Wu has a bag, and pass food and water down
strings.让它闻到活人的味道: Let it smell that there are living people down here
strings.让朵朵喊：孩子的声音最尖，传得最远: Let Daisy shout: a child's voice is shrillest and carries furthest
strings.让秦朗管：结构上的事，听懂行的: Let Leonard Qin run it: on structure, listen to the one who knows
strings.让老乡老刘活着出去: Get Dustin, your neighbour from back home, out alive
strings.让领头人把水桶看起来，谁也不许碰: Have the leader keep the jug where no one can touch it
strings.讲一个自己的故事: Tell a story of your own
strings.讲义气、嘴碎、自来熟，对“老板”有本能的反感；吃得了苦，最见不得人欺负老实人。: Loyal to his own, mouthy, friendly with everybody; instinctively allergic to bosses. He can take hardship, and he can’t stand watching anyone push a decent man around.
strings.讲故事、聊家里的事、给伤员喂水擦汗、提醒别人别睡死过去。不出力，但能让大家熬得住: Tell stories, talk about home, hold water to the injured and wipe the sweat off them, keep people from sliding into a sleep they won’t wake from. No heavy work — but it is what holds everyone together.
strings.证据就没了——如果没被她发现的话: The evidence is gone — if she doesn’t catch you
strings.话不多，手很稳。见过太多死人，所以对活人格外有耐心，相信“只要人还在说话，就有希: He doesn’t say much, and his hands are steady. He has seen too many dead, and is therefore especially patient with the living — he believes that as long as a person is still talking, there is hope. Sometimes he goes quiet without warning: he is remembering his own three days under the house.
strings.说什么都没用。老刘把嘴闭得死死的。: Nothing works. Dustin keeps his mouth shut tight.
strings.说出违规加盖和那张验收单: Say it: the illegally added floors, and the acceptance certificate
strings.说话慢条斯理，爱用数字：“按现在这个喝法，水还能撑三天半。”: She speaks slowly and precisely, and reaches for numbers: “At the rate we’re drinking, the water lasts three and a half more days.”
strings.说话简短，像下命令，偶尔冒出部队腔：“收到”“注意安全”。: Short sentences, like orders. Army habits surface now and then: “Copy that.” “Stay safe.”
strings.说话要费口水和力气，但能让两边都撑得久一点: Talking costs spit and strength, but it keeps both sides holding on longer
strings.请他跟上面说：先别吊，换个慢法子一点点凿: Ask him to tell them: don’t lift — go slow, chisel it out
strings.谁也不多吃亏；可每个人都会更渴一点: Nobody loses much; everyone ends up a little thirstier
strings.谁也别动，等它自己停下来: Nobody moves. Wait for it to stop on its own
strings.谁当头照旧，秦朗出主意就行: Leadership stays as it is; Leonard Qin advises
strings.谁抽屉里的一盒头孢: A box of cephalosporin from someone’s drawer
strings.谁都想早一分钟看见天: Everyone wants to see the sky one minute sooner
strings.调查组后来请秦朗去讲那几天的事。他把三角区里每一根桌腿的位置都画了出来，标着哪一: The investigators later asked Leonard Qin to walk them through those days. He drew the position of every table leg in the triangle and marked which ones he had striped with lipstick. Someone asked if he had been afraid. Yes, he said. When I was afraid, I went and tapped those table legs.
strings.谨慎、精于算计、话少，凡事先算账；对何志强又怕又恨；一提到儿子，整个人就会突然软: Cautious, calculating, sparing with words; she counts the cost of everything first. She fears Steven Ho and resents him in equal measure. Mention her son and she goes soft all at once.
strings.费点力气，至少能知道她怎么样了: Costs some strength, but at least you will know how she is
strings.趁他一个人，按住他，把他身上的水和吃的留下: Get him alone, pin him down, and keep his water and food
strings.趁他发愣，把袋子里的手机和充电宝都拿过来给大家用: While he is dazed, take the phones and power banks from the sack for everyone to use
strings.趁压得还不久，挤压综合征的风险小；可板子一动，头顶可能跟着塌，撬不动还会砸伤人: Crush syndrome is a smaller risk while he hasn’t been pinned long; but move that slab and the ceiling may come with it — and if the lever slips it will crush someone
strings.趁她睡着，偷偷翻她的包: Wait until she’s asleep and search the bag
strings.趁还有力气把能用的东西都扒出来；老刘先晾着: Get everything usable out while there is still strength to do it; Dustin waits
strings.趁还没漏光，每个人现在先喝个够: Drink your fill now, before it all drains away
strings.跟一个小偷做交易；他也许会守信: A deal with a thief; he might keep his word
strings.跟她一起喊：“这里有人！还有个孩子！”: Shout with her: “There are people here! There’s a child!”
strings.跟她约好：每隔一阵互相敲三下，省点力气: Agree with her: knock three times every so often, save the strength
strings.跟她谈：出去以后给她一笔钱，让她自己删: Make her a deal: money once they’re out, if she deletes it herself
strings.跟着何志强干了八年的老财务。单亲妈妈，儿子在读初中。右脚踝扭伤了，一直把一个黑色: The veteran accountant who has kept Steven Ho’s books for eight years. A single mother with a son in middle school. Her right ankle is sprained, and she has not once loosened her grip on the black briefcase against her chest.
strings.身体好的人先出去，给里面腾地方: The healthy go first, to make room inside
strings.身体好的人先爬了出去。留在最后的人，听着头顶的脚步声越来越远。: The strong ones climb out. Those left for last listen to the footsteps overhead grow fainter.
strings.转头把秦朗的事告诉何志强——自己的事也就瞒不住了: Turn and tell Steven Ho about Leonard Qin — which means her own business comes out too
strings.轮流留一部手机开着，等信号进来: Leave one phone on at all times, waiting for a signal
strings.过了很久，一个塑料袋从裂缝里一点点塞了下来：半瓶水，一盒饼干，一部还剩四分之一电: After a long time a plastic bag comes down through the crack, a little at a time: half a bottle of water, a box of biscuits, a phone with a quarter of its charge left. On the back of the phone case is a sticker: “Happy Teacher’s Day, Teacher Wu.” Above, the crying gets louder than before.
strings.还没到那一步: It hasn’t come to that yet
strings.这一回合挖掘、撬动造成的结构松动，结算时折算成三角区完好度的损失。: How much this round’s digging and prying has loosened the structure; converted into lost triangle integrity at the end of the round.
strings.这一次让她喝个够，以后就顾不上了: Let her drink her fill this once; after that, nothing more
strings.这一次，缝终于撬开了。朵朵被几只手从缝里接了下来，浑身发烫，搂住第一个碰到的人的: This time the crack opens. Daisy is handed down through it, burning hot, and she clamps her arms round the first neck she reaches and will not let go.
strings.这件事暂时没有下文。: For now, nothing comes of it.
strings.这句话，何志强最怕别人问: It is the one question Steven Ho dreads
strings.这块板子我看过了，吃得住劲儿。放心睡。: I’ve had a look at this slab. It’ll hold. Go to sleep.
strings.这栋楼的 11、12 层是房东前年违规加盖的，没做过结构验算。加盖楼层的装修就是: The 11th and 12th floors of this building were added illegally by the landlord two years ago, without any structural review. Your company did the fit-out of those floors, and the acceptance certificate bears your signature; the “inspection fee” for the quality-control office was delivered by your accountant on your orders. Last month your intern Lily Lin photographed a diagonal crack in the pantry wall and sent it to you. You replied: “Don’t go spreading this in the group chat. It looks bad.”
strings.这楼原先只有十层。上头那两层是前年加的，我那阵在对面工地搬砖，看着他们一层一层往: This building only had ten floors to start with. The top two went on the year before last. I was lugging bricks on the site opposite, and I watched them stack them up, one on top of another.
strings.这楼我熟。管道井底下通车库，车库塌了一半，另一半还立着。: I know this building. The pipe shaft comes out by the garage. Half the garage is down; the other half is still standing.
strings.远处传来挖掘机的轰鸣，还有扩音器断断续续的喊声：“……下面……有没有人……”救援: Somewhere off in the distance comes the rumble of excavators and a megaphone voice breaking up: “…below… is anyone…” The rescue teams have reached the district! But several buildings around you are down — which one will they search first?
strings.追究还有什么用: What good would it do now?
strings.通道打通的时候，冯建军已经不在了。救援队员把他从碎块底下抬出来，盖上了一面队旗。: By the time the tunnel was through, Jim Feng was gone. The rescuers carried him out from under the debris and laid a team flag over him. Alive: {survivors}. Never came out: {dead}. His teammates said afterwards that Old Feng had one line he kept coming back to all his life: in ’76 somebody dug him out of the ground, and he owed that life back. He paid it.
strings.通道挖到一半，外面的人先凿通了一条窄缝，窄得只能侧着身子一寸一寸地挪。过了一会儿: Halfway through cutting the tunnel, the crews outside break through a narrow slit — so narrow you have to go sideways, an inch at a time. A while later a lean, tall man forces himself through it, the lamp on his yellow helmet blinding: “Don’t be scared, don’t be scared. My name’s Feng. I came from Tangshan.” In his pack are two litres of water, an IV set and two bags of saline. “These two bags are all the saline there is. Who goes on first?”
strings.遗物里有一块表，指针停在两点四十一分。他老婆把表擦干净，放进了骨灰盒。宏远的老员: Among his effects was a watch, its hands stopped at 2:41. His wife wiped it clean and laid it in the urn. Later, when the old staff of Hongyuan spoke of Mr Ho, they always sighed first, and then said nothing more.
strings.那个U盘最后被她交给了调查组。她作为证人出了两次庭，把八年的账一笔一笔念出来，念: In the end she handed the drive to the investigation team. She testified twice, reading out eight years of accounts, one entry at a time; halfway through she stopped for a sip of water. Her son’s surgery was paid for by crowdfunding, and the page read: “His mother was once buried under the rubble of an earthquake.”
strings.那个圈转了一遍又一遍，最后跳出来一个红色的感叹号。: The little circle spins and spins, and then a red exclamation mark appears.
strings.那个开挖掘机的叔叔后来找到了朵朵家。他说那天他就是听见了一个小姑娘喊自己的名字，: The man who drove the excavator came to Daisy's home later. He said it was because he heard a little girl shouting her own name that he stopped the bucket that day. Daisy asked: "Was I loud?" He said: "Loud. The whole world heard you."
strings.那个掰断的U盘再也没人找到。调查组找他谈过两次，他都说“记不清了”。宏远换了个名: The broken USB drive was never found. The investigation talked to him twice; both times he said he “couldn’t remember”. Hongyuan changed its name and kept winning contracts. Only, from then on, he never took a meeting in a room with a suspended ceiling — the first thing he does on walking into one is find the load-bearing columns.
strings.那天从三角区里出来的人，是一个一个躺着上的担架，胳膊上都挂着盐水。冯建军在洞口数: Everyone who came out of the triangle that day came out lying on a stretcher with a drip in their arm. Jim Feng counted them out at the mouth of the hole and only let himself be pulled up after the last one. On the road home to Tangshan he phoned the village where his uncle is buried and said: Uncle, this time nobody died coming out.
strings.那天他被喊出去以后，就再也没能钻回来——楼板吊开以后，通道换了方向。他在外面守到: After he was called out that day he never managed to get back in — once the slab was lifted, the passage changed direction. He stayed outside until the last person was carried out of the triangle, then, without going over to say anything, turned and went to the next building. Years later someone recognised him in a documentary about the Tangshan earthquake.
strings.那年六月十八号，黄勇穿着骑手服，去了一个陌生人的婚礼。他在门口找到新娘，把陈阿姨: On the eighteenth of June that year Ken Huang, in his delivery jacket, went to a stranger's wedding. He found the bride at the door and told her Auntie Chen's words one at a time: the tin box, under the bed, buy the dress. The wedding dress the bride was wearing had been bought.
strings.那边咕咚咕咚地喝了很久。最后她说：“够了，够了，你们留着。”: On the other side she drinks for a long time. In the end she says: "That's enough, enough. Keep the rest."
strings.部队的老战友来送他，在灵堂外站成一排，敬了个礼。他们说秦朗当工兵那几年，拆过的危: His old comrades came to see him off; they stood in a row outside the funeral hall and saluted. They said that in his years as a combat engineer Leonard Qin had taken down more condemned buildings than anyone — “he knew better than anyone which slab wouldn’t hold.”
strings.都熬到这时候了，能爬的自己爬，快点出去: After all this? Anyone who can climb climbs out on their own, as fast as possible
strings.里面越空，医生越好干活: The emptier it is in here, the better the doctor can work
strings.针扎进去的时候，朵朵咬着嘴唇，一声都没哭。冯建军竖起大拇指：“好样的，比我孙子强: When the needle goes in, Daisy bites her lip and doesn’t cry at all. Jim Feng gives her a thumbs-up: “Good girl. Braver than my grandson.”
strings.钢管敲在柱子上的声音，在废墟里响了整整一夜。: The sound of steel on the column rang through the ruin all night.
strings.钢管敲在柱子上，“当、当、当”，一轮接一轮，敲到虎口震裂。: Steel pipe on concrete, clang, clang, clang, round after round, until the webs of their hands split.
strings.钢管敲在柱子上，“当、当、当”，停一停，再“当、当、当”。: Steel on concrete: clang, clang, clang — pause — clang, clang, clang.
strings.钱还没拿到，东西先没了: The money isn’t in hand, and the thing is already gone
strings.问他：要不要用这部手机，给侄儿家里报个信: Ask him if he wants to use this phone to get word to his nephew's family
strings.阿姨，你身上的味道跟我妈妈好像。: Auntie, you smell like my mum.
strings.隔壁已经大半天没有动静了。上一次敲墙，墙那边没有回应。: There has been no sound from next door for most of a day now. Last time you knocked, nothing came back.
strings.隔着墙跟她说话，大家轮流陪她: Talk to her through the wall; everyone takes turns keeping her company
strings.隔着墙，一个字一个字地复述给她听，让她放心: Repeat it back to her through the wall, word for word, so she can rest easy
strings.雨伞倒挂在裂缝下面，水滴进去的声音，是这几天最好听的声音。: The umbrella hangs inverted under the crack, and the sound of water dropping into it is the best sound in days.
strings.雨水顺着楼板的裂缝往下渗，滴答滴答，空气里一股水泥和霉味。: Rain seeps down through the cracks in the slab, drip by drip. The air smells of cement and mildew.
strings.雨水顺着楼板的裂缝渗了进来，一滴一滴落在会议桌上，汇成了一小滩。: Rainwater seeps in through the cracks in the slab, drop by drop onto the conference table, gathering into a small pool.
strings.震后基站大面积损毁，应急通信车和抢修会让信号慢慢恢复。: Cell towers across the area were wrecked in the quake; emergency communication trucks and repairs will slowly bring the signal back.
strings.震后第八天，黄金救援期早已过去，大型机械开始一层层清理锦华大厦的废墟。挖掘机的铲: On the eighth day after the quake the golden window was long past, and heavy machinery had begun stripping Jinhua Tower down, floor by floor. When the excavator bucket stopped at the third floor, the operator heard faint knocking underneath. Lifted out: {survivors}. Did not live to see it: {dead}.
strings.静听的时候，敲击声最清楚: In the listening silence, knocking carries clearest
strings.顺着半塌的楼梯间，你们一寸一寸地往上爬，钢筋划破了衣服和手掌。最后一个人钻出来的: Up through the half-collapsed stairwell you climb an inch at a time, rebar tearing clothes and palms. When the last one comes out, the rescuers on the road stare for several seconds before they run to help. Then they follow the way you crawled, and go back in for the people still inside. Alive: {survivors}. Never came out: {dead}.
strings.顺着狗洞往外掏，让风进来: Dig outward along the dog hole, let the air in
strings.领头人管水——前提是大家信得过他: The leader controls the water — if they still trust him
strings.领带、丝巾、袜子……能捂嘴的都用上了。: Ties, scarves, socks… anything that can cover a mouth is pressed into service.
strings.马上撬开：拿会议桌腿当撬棍，大家一起使劲: Pry it off now: use a table leg as a crowbar and everyone heaves together
strings.马上给 119 发短信：楼名、楼层、几个人、谁受了伤: Text 119 right now: tower name, floor, how many people, who is injured
strings.黄色的液压顶杆一点点撑开了楼板。老刘被抬起来的时候，所有人都围在他身边，谁也没有: The yellow hydraulic ram opens the slab a little at a time. As Dustin is lifted, everyone is around him. No one has gone first.
strings.黑暗里，头顶那道斜裂缝里断断续续传来细细的哭声，像猫叫。大家屏住呼吸听了很久，才: Out of the dark, from the slanted crack overhead, comes thin broken crying, like a kitten. Everyone holds their breath and listens for a long time before the words are clear: “Mama… I want my mama…” A child. She says her name is Daisy; she was napping at the after-school center on the fourth floor, and Teacher Wu picked her up and ran, and then Teacher Wu stopped talking, and her hand was so cold.
strings.黑暗里，秦朗凑到周敏耳边：“交易还作数。五十万，出去以后一分不少。现在先把东西给: In the dark, Leonard Qin leans close to Michelle Zhou’s ear: “The offer still stands. Half a million, not a cent less, once we’re out. Give me the thing now — what if you don’t get out?”
strings.黑瘦，戴一顶沾满灰的安全帽，帽檐上绑着头灯，背着一个鼓鼓囊囊的蛇皮袋，手里攥着一: Wiry and dark, in a dust-caked hard hat with a headlamp strapped to the brim, a bulging woven sack on his back and a crowbar in his fist. He came up through the pipe shaft from the underground garage behind the tower, climbing floor by floor through the wreckage. He says he is looking for his nephew, who worked in the building — but the sack holds phones, laptops and a few wallets. He worked on demolition crews when he was younger, and he knows where you can crawl into a collapsed building and what you must not touch.
strings.（冯建军把头盔上的灯拧暗了一点：“省着点电，后面还用得上。”）: (Jim Feng dims the lamp on his helmet. “Save the battery. We’ll need it later.”)
strings.（后来大家才知道：那天中午，一条脖子上缠着胶带的黄狗冲进了街口的救援帐篷，咬着一: (Only later did they learn: that midday, a yellow dog with tape round its neck ran into the rescue tent at the corner of the street, took a rescuer’s trouser leg in its teeth and kept dragging him toward Jinhua Tower.)
strings.（后来大家才知道：那天天还没亮，一个浑身是灰的瘦子跑到救援指挥部，说锦华大厦三楼: (Only later did they learn: before dawn that day, a dust-covered thin man ran to the rescue command post, said there were living people on the east side of the third floor of Jinhua Tower, and disappeared into the crowd.)
strings.（很多天以后，救援队在四楼的夹缝里找到了吴老师和朵朵。吴老师的两只胳膊，还环在孩: (Many days later, the rescue teams found Teacher Wu and Daisy in the gap on the fourth floor. Teacher Wu’s arms were still around the child.)
strings.（来福在西北角刨了一阵，鼻子贴着碎砖使劲嗅，又跑回老刘身边。）: (Buddy digs for a while in the northwest corner, nose pressed to the broken bricks, then trots back to Dustin.)
strings.（来福忽然竖起耳朵，冲着头顶的裂缝低低地呜了一声。）: (Buddy suddenly pricks up his ears and whines low at the crack overhead.)
strings.（来福把下巴搁在老刘的胸口上，一动不动地盯着他的脸。）: (Buddy rests his chin on Dustin’s chest and stares at his face without moving.)
strings.（来福的舌头耷拉在外面，喘得很急。它已经很久没有叫过了。）: (Buddy’s tongue hangs out; he is panting hard. He hasn’t barked in a long time.)
strings.（来福舔了舔地上一小滩水渍，又抬头看了看水桶。）: (Buddy laps at a little puddle on the floor, then looks up at the water jug.)
strings.（爬出去的人一出车库口就昏了过去，被抬上救护车的时候，嘴里只反复念着两个字：“三: (The one who crawled out passed out the moment they were clear of the garage; on the way to the ambulance, the only words they kept repeating were: “Third floor… third floor…”)
strings.（老陶从车库钻出去以后，在警戒线外面站了很久，最后背着蛇皮袋走了。）: (After Tom got out through the garage he stood outside the cordon for a long time, and then walked off with the sack on his back.)
strings.（老陶蹲在检修口旁边，手里一直捏着一根没点的烟。）: (Tom squats by the access hatch, rolling an unlit cigarette between his fingers.)
strings.（那之后，再也没有人听见过墙那边的声音。）: (After that, no one ever hears anything through that wall again.)
strings.（黑暗里，来福挨着谁的腿趴了下来，身上热乎乎的。）: (In the dark, Buddy lies down against someone’s leg, his body warm.)
